OF THE SECOND SONG

That even without usurpation, Christ Jesus claimed for himself all the divine names. <note>original: "absque rapina" — a reference to Philippians 2:6, where Christ "did not count equality with God something to be grasped" or "robbery."</note>

### Chapter VI.

<margin>We do not dare to speak of the divine names, except insofar as we have received them as revealed.</margin>
**C**oming now to supramundane <note>beyond the physical world</note> things, although God is unique and most especially one, he is nevertheless called by many names. These are not intended to express multiple essences or deities within him, but rather his properties. While these properties emanate from the same source of deity and remain always one at their root, they are spoken of as many in relation to us, upon whom many benefits and diverse gifts trickle down through various channels. Therefore, God himself, though most unified, is assigned various names, of which Jerome <note>St. Jerome (c. 347–420 AD), the translator of the Vulgate Bible.</note> <margin>Jerome</margin> compiled a brief work of ten names addressed to Marcella. Dionysius <note>Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagita, a mystical theologian whose "On the Divine Names" was highly influential.</note> <margin>Dionysius</margin> however, proceeding further, collects forty-five names of God and of our Christ. Indeed, the Hebrew doctors <margin>Hebrew Teachers</margin> derive seventy-two names from a certain text found in the fourteenth <margin>Exodus</margin> chapter of Exodus, based on a name of seventy-two letters <note>This refers to the "Shem HaMephorash," a hidden name of God derived by Kabbalists from Exodus 14:19-21.</note>. Others, however, going even further, suggest so many divine names that both their number and what they signify are entirely unknown to us. Yet each man speaks according to his own capacity, because not all secrets are revealed to everyone. Nor would we dare to say anything about these names except insofar as they have been revealed to us by God through his kindness, as Dionysius <margin>Dionysius</margin> teaches us, and with him other wise men—not only Catholics and Hebrews, but even Plato, who in the *Cratylus* says: Divine names were held by the "barbarians," <margin>Plato</margin> that is, the Hebrews, who received them from God. Without God, we can in no way grasp the true discourses and true names by which God is called. Therefore, as far as the divine light shall shine upon us, we will touch upon some of these names, all of which apply to Christ. We do this, however, by that law which Dionysius <margin>Dionysius</margin> teaches: that we should by no means presume to explain that supreme and ineffable <note>unutterable or beyond description</note> substance, which neither sense, nor imagination, nor speech, nor touch, nor our knowledge can reach. For the deity is unnamable, above-named, and <term>supersubstantial</term> <note>meaning "beyond essence" or existing in a way that transcends the human category of "being."</note>; it is contained in the most remote recess of its own divinity and solitary retreat, hiding itself in the abyss of its own darkness. In the supersubstantial <term>thearchy</term> <note>the source of divinity or divine rule</note>, it is excellently separated from every habit, motion, deliberation, name, word, intellect, placement, station, and end, entirely fleeing our knowledge and exposition. The Hebrews call this the infinite cause of causes <margin>Hebrews</margin> and the substance above all substance. Nor do they presume to speak anything else of it, because it is infinite and in no way perceivable by our intellect. This is the one whom (unless I am mistaken) Isaiah <margin>Isaiah</margin> wished not to explain, but barely to hint at by a certain general term when he introduces him speaking these words: **"I am the Lord: that is my name; and my glory I will not give to another"** <note>original Hebrew: "אני יהוה הוא שמי וכבודי לאחר לא אתן" (Isaiah 42:8)</note>. That is, "I am the Lord," namely: *That which is*, is my name; "this glory of mine I will not give to another," or to one foreign to me. In place of this, our translation <note>The Latin Vulgate</note> has: "This is my name," so that the relative "this" seems to refer to some specific name; yet it indicates no specific name, but only hints at that which is in the highest degree, and...

# THE SIXTH TONE.

We shall speak with reverence, because this name is above all names expressing attributes or particular properties. For just as the Father gave all things to him, so he also granted him a name that carries all those things within it, so that the name itself is fitting to the one named. Let us briefly run through the great skill with which all things are included in the name <note>The author likely refers to a Hebrew or symbolic spelling of the name Jesus, such as YHS (יהש) or Yod-He-Shin-Vav-Ayin</note>. Among those who are skilled in **formal arithmetic**, a simple number indicates divine things; a ten indicates celestial things; a hundred indicates the grosser and corruptible things; but a thousand refers again to divine things and to God, whom finally <margin>Song of Songs</margin> all things seek. Therefore, at the end of the Song of Songs, it is said: *A thousand for you, Solomon*—that is, for you who are your own peace—*and two hundred for those who keep its fruit*; that is, for us living in corruptible flesh, who seek to keep his commandments, from which we take the fruits of eternal life. 

The wise Hebrews follow this teaching when they declare the mystery of that <term>teruma</term> <note>A Hebrew word for a "heave offering" or "contribution" given to the priests</note>, which we call a tithe: in which the hundredth part belongs to the people; the tenth part, which is the tithe of the hundred, was given to the priests as men who are certainly celestial; and the tenth of this ten—which is one—was given to God. See, therefore, that the simpler number is given to God, the hundred to the thicker sort of people who are still unrefined and subject to corruption, but the ten to the priests who mediate between the two. 

All these things are understood to be concluded in the name **Jesus**: for it is composed of three letters, of which one carries a simple <gloss>number</gloss> <note>original: "numerum"</note> (specifically the letter **Vav** <note>original: "ו"</note> which stands for 6); another, which is **Yod** <note>original: "י"</note>, signifies ten; while another, namely **Shin** <note>original: "ש"</note>, includes the hundreds. Nor should it be wondered at if the letter representing the number does not refer to unity, but to the number six, because this was not done without a sacred mystery. For since the Supreme Architect entered into the fabric of the world through the number six—a number that is primarily "perfect" <note>In classical mathematics, a perfect number is equal to the sum of its proper divisors; 1+2+3=6</note>—it is fitting that it be included in the name of the Word Incarnate, through whom all things were made. 

But regarding the great mystery of how he went forth into the fabric of the world through the number six, besides those things said elsewhere, we shall touch upon these few points. The <term>Monad</term> <note>The number one, representing unity or God</note> is supremely one and fruitful; therefore it produces another, from which the **binary** <note>the number two</note> arises. Between the producer and the produced there is a mutual relationship, and behold, we have the **ternary** <note>the number three</note>. Now, combine these three and they will give the number six; for in doing so, one and two make three; if three are added to these, they make six. 

The first ternary, gathered from the producer, the produced, and the mutual relationship (or reciprocal love), is in God. The other ternary, however, is in created things, since all things contain a trace of God even in number: for they have **matter** and **form**, from which results the **composite**, which they call a certain third thing. <margin>Angels have their own matter and composition</margin> Nor should one object regarding the Angels, because they also have their own matter and their own composition. There is also another ternary in every single creature, <gloss>namely</gloss> <note>original: "v3"</note> a beginning, a middle, and an end. 

And it is well that among the letters signifying numbers in the name of **Jesus**, the **Yod** <note>original: "י"</note> is placed, by which the **Tree of Life** is designated, since he himself was that very Tree of Life, giving life to all. See, therefore, how beautifully it is indicated in this name of Jesus that all things were included in the one named, as the Apostle says: <margin>Paul</margin> "Because it pleased the Father <gloss>namely</gloss> that all fullness should dwell in him, and through him..."

It would be far too long to write about all these things, and we would wander further than the present work requires. However, we shall outline how the principal names of God—those most frequently and openly repeated in Holy Scripture—are contained in this name ישו <note>original: "Iesu" / the three-letter Hebrew form Y-S-V</note>. This four-letter name <note>The Tetragrammaton, יהוה</note> is the most celebrated and frequent, which is written thus: יהוה <note>Yod-He-Vav-He</note> and cannot be expressed; but when it is read, it is pronounced as **Adonai** <note>meaning "Lord"</note>.

<margin>The same</margin>
Thus, two principal letters of this name, namely י <note>Yod</note> and ו <note>Vav</note>, are contained in the name ישו <note>Iesu</note>. Truly, the two ה <note>He</note> letters are changed by a very great mystery into the letter ש <note>Shin</note>. For the more secret theologians <note>A reference to Christian Kabbalists or students of Jewish mysticism</note> say that God, the highest craftsman, produced all spiritual things through a certain power signified in the first ה, but bodily things through the power signified in the second ה.

<margin>The same</margin>
And since all things were brought into being through the Word made human, who is named **Jesus**, those very powers or properties signified by those two ה letters are included within him. But because Jesus was given and sent to us as a redeemer and a leader to true rest—which is eternal life—and indeed was made into our rest itself, therefore, in place of those two ה letters (which signify the principles of the beginning), there is placed in the name ישו <note>Iesu</note> the letter ש <note>Shin</note>. This letter is the beginning of the word שבת <note>Sabbath</note> and signifies the word itself, which is interpreted as **rest**.

Behold how many and how great are the mysteries imported into the three letters of this name ישו [IESU]: For י <note>Yod</note> signifies divinity (as is very well known among those same theologians) as well as the **Tree of Life**, and ו <note>Vav</note> signifies rest. It is denoted that our Jesus is God, giving life to all with both kinds of life <note>referring to physical and spiritual life</note>, and finally blessing them in that eternal rest. That four-letter name <note>the Tetragrammaton</note> also exists in the name of Jesus through another mystery—namely, by way of numbers <term>Gematria</term> <note>The practice of assigning numerical values to letters to find hidden connections between words</note>—when the name of his mother is added, from whom he drew the substance of his body. For the four letters of that name <note>יהוה</note> return the number 26; and the name of his mother, which is מרים <note>Miriam/Mary</note>, gives 290. This number, joined with that 26, constitutes 316—which is the same number given by the letters of the name ישו <note>I-S-V: 10 + 300 + 6 = 316</note>. In this, it is denoted that the one named proceeded from both God the Father and a human mother.

By this same path of numbers, we conclude that the terrifying name שדי <note>Shadai / The Almighty</note> is enclosed within Jesus. Its letters in number give 314. If to this number the digit two is added—which signifies "embodiment" or "corporality"—it constitutes 316, which is the number of the letters of the name ישו <note>Iesu</note>, as we just said. Also, the power of that name שדי <note>Shadai</note> was given to him, which was always terrifying to the enemies of the human race.

<margin>David</margin>

Hence, in the fabric of the world, when God—by diffusing Himself into creatures—began to appear as manifold, He is introduced as the creator under this name **Elohim** <note>original: "Elohim"; a Hebrew name for God that is grammatically plural but used with singular verbs in the Bible</note>, as the Scripture says: *And Elohim said / and Elohim made, and Elohim created*. Others, however, join a singular name with a singular verb, saying that through this is understood the Trinity and the plurality of Persons. But in a true and proper exposition, through that name **Elohim** is understood the **Craftsman** <term>opifex</term> <note>The divine "maker" or architect of the universe</note> diffusing Himself into many things, or the one judging many through various ministers who execute His judgment. Hence, in Scripture, sometimes even the Angels who execute God's judgments and the judges who judge <margin>Exodus</margin> are called **Elohim**, as we find in Exodus, when thieves and those who cause damage are ordered to be brought to the **Elohim** so that they may be judged by them; where our translation has: *the cause of these men shall come before the gods.* <note>Referencing Exodus 22:9, where "Elohim" is often translated as "judges" in this legal context</note>

Therefore, not only do the virtues of these names—which are to show mercy, to distribute, and to judge—agree in our Jesus, but so do the mysteries of the letters. If we wished to declare these, I fear we might travel further than is permitted to write or speak; nevertheless, we shall run through something on the surface. In this name, therefore, the first letter is א <note>Aleph</note>, which, when expanded into its component letters by saying <term>Aleph</term> <note>Hebrew: אלף (Aleph-Lamed-Pe)</note>, signifies "one thousand." We have already declared this attribute to belong to our **Solomon** <note>A symbolic name for Christ as the Prince of Peace</note>, who is peace unto himself and the true Peaceful King. Truly, if the number of those three letters is calculated, a great mystery still arises: <gloss>30</gloss> for ל <note>Lamed</note> gives 30, <gloss>300</gloss> for פ <note>Pe</note> <note>The text assigns 300 to Pe here, though in standard Hebrew it is 80; this likely follows a specific mystical or symbolic system used by the author</note>, and <gloss>1</gloss> for א <note>Aleph</note> gives one. These numbers joined together return a three: namely, a three-hundred, a ten <note>original: "denarium," referring to the place value of tens</note>, and a unit, about which we spoke above.

And if one pays attention to the shapes <note>original: "characteres"</note> of the numbers, the mystery will be even more apparent. For there are three strokes emanating from one character <note>A reference to the visual form of the letter Aleph (א), often seen as a diagonal bar with two smaller strokes</note>, which implies "one," so that it may be hinted that the Trinity of Persons proceeds from and is contained within one Unity; just as in pronouncing the letter א itself, it is necessary that we expand it into those three aforementioned letters <note>A-L-P</note>. We have, therefore, in the letter א the mystery of the unique Deity and the Trinity. 

But to this is added ל <note>Lamed</note>, which signifies 30 in number—that is, three tens—to denote the celestial power fortified by the most holy Trinity, through which God, as if through secondary causes, disposes all lower things. It is clear that all these things are found in Christ Jesus. For **JESUS** is the **Beginning** signified by the א, just as he himself <margin>CHRIST.</margin> testifies, saying: *I am the beginning, who speaks to you.* <note>A reference to the Latin Vulgate's translation of John 8:25</note> And the logic of the Trinity is in him, when he says of the Father: *The Father is in me*; and again: *I and the Father are one.* Concerning the Holy Spirit, he also says: *He shall receive of mine.* From these we gather that the logic of the Trinity and the "Beginning" are in him, whence the name importing those two things is appropriate for him. 

From here we can also infer how the power of the supreme name is contained in Jesus. For that name is **Ehyeh** <note>original: "אהיה" / "I AM," the name God gave Moses at the burning bush</note>, beginning from א and containing י <note>Yod</note> and a double ה <note>He</note>. By this, for those who know the mysteries of letters, the first Beginning and the ultimate End are denoted, since it signifies "one" and "one thousand," which is the cube of ten and of the final simple number. Similarly, י <note>Yod</note> implies the Beginning, just as its interpretation indicates...

### Chapter VIII. Why only the name of Jesus is invoked today by true worshippers of God.

<margin>Zechariah</margin> Since we have declared that all names and all kinds of powers enclosed within them are found in **Jesus** and his name, we rightly invoke this name alone, according to the prophecy of **Zechariah**, where he says: *And the Lord shall be king over all the earth, and in that day there shall be one Lord, and his name one.* <note>Zechariah 14:9</note> Nor is anyone found who has been king of the whole earth and Lord, except **Jesus**, under whom, after idolatry was destroyed, all held him as King and Lord—except for a few dispersed Hebrews—until that beast **Mohammed** <note>original: "Mahumeth"</note> arose. Nevertheless, no other name has been given to men by which they might be saved except the <margin>Peter</margin> name of **Jesus**, as **Peter** said in the Acts of the Apostles. He commanded this name to be spread among all nations, just as the four-letter name was formerly known only among the <margin>**CHRIST.**</margin> people of Israel. For he said to **Ananias** concerning **Paul**: *This man is a chosen vessel to me, to carry my name before the Gentiles, and kings, and the children of Israel.* <note>Acts 9:15</note> This he did: for immediately he went from **Damascus** to **Jerusalem**, then to **Tarsus** of **Cilicia** (the capital), then to the noble city of **Antioch** in **Syria**. Afterward, he went to **Phrygia**, **Galatia**, **Troas**, **Macedonia**, and **Athens**, where the wisdom of the world flourished. After these, he went to **Corinth**, **Ephesus**, **Miletus**, **Cos**, **Rhodes**, and traveling further through those islands of **Achaia** and **Greece**, he proceeded to the **Arabs** and came to **Italy**. He traveled as far as the **Spaniards** through **Asia** and **Europe**, carrying and making known the name of **Jesus**. And what remained of the world, the other Apostles filled with the power of this name, so that all people and all things could ask in the name of **Jesus**, just as he himself taught, saying: *Whatever you ask the Father in my name, he will give it to you.* <note>John 16:23</note> <margin>The same Paul</margin> The power of this name is so great that all can be enriched by it, as **Paul** says: *He is rich toward all who call upon him,* <note>Romans 10:12</note> that is, the name **JESUS**, which is so gentle, so communicable, and so <margin>Song of Songs</margin> diffusive of itself that it is compared to oil in the **Song of Songs**, where it says: *Your name is oil poured out,* <note>original: "Oleum effusum nomen tuum"; Song of Songs 1:3</note> because its power, full of anointing, is spread into those whom it touches, like oil in a cloth; and because it heals, and seasons, and does all things.

The first letters of these words, placed in Hebrew order, are **YHWH**, **YHW**, and **YSU** <note>יהוה יהו ישׁו — showing the transition from the Name of God to the Name of Jesus</note>. 

But after we have treated the letters of the name of **Jesus**, I thought it opportune to explain also that, from the interpretation of the letters, more letters ought not to be found in it, since these perfectly convey those things which are contained in the one named by this name **YSU** (ישׁו): For **Y** signifies the Beginning; **S** denotes the Sabbath, hinting at rest and the end. They denote, therefore, that he himself is the Beginning, the End, and the Rest of all things, just as in the <margin>Revelation</margin> Apocalypse he says himself: *I am the Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end.* And since all things are included in these words, those letters suffice, nor should others be added. Furthermore, this name **YSU** (ישׁו) is completed from the major, minor, and middle numbers into a **ten**, which is a complete number. For there is a six <note>The letter Vav (ו)</note>, one ten <note>The letter Yod (י)</note>, and three hundreds <note>The letter Shin (ש)</note>, which joined together constitute ten <note>The author is using a form of digital reduction or mystical arithmetic where the total values (300+10+6) are reduced or related to the number 10</note>, a number indeed perfect and constituted from all kinds of things: spiritual <term>yz</term>, celestial, and terrestrial, which are conveyed by units, tens, and hundreds, <margin>Paul</margin> according to that which **Paul** frequently repeats, saying: *In him is all fullness, and in him all things are reconciled.* 

But leaving aside lower things so that we may speak of higher ones, I say that all the supernal waters of graces and gifts are collected in him, as if in the true "upper pool," of which it is said in the <margin>Song of Songs</margin> Canticles: *Thine eyes are like the fishpools in Heshbon*—that is, in thought or in the word, in which all things were contained before they were created. For **Heshbon** <note>Hebrew: חֶשְׁבּוֹן</note> signifies "thoughts" as applied to the Word. Whence where we have *In the beginning was the Word*, in the Hebrew it has: *In the beginning was the thought* <note>original: "beresit haiah hesbon"; Hebrew: בְּרֵאשִׁית הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה — the author is making a mystical pun on the place name Heshbon and the Hebrew root for thought/calculation</note>, that is, there was the thought, the word, the pool, in which all things were contained before they were created. It is therefore the true **Probatic Pool** <note>The pool at the Sheep Gate in Jerusalem (John 5:2), believed to have healing powers</note>, in which all the sheep must be washed who are to be placed at the right hand of the Supreme Judge. This pool was prefigured by that which was in the earthly Jerusalem, in which every single person was healed, whoever they were and by whatever infirmity they were held, because by a single principle of healing in the Divine Word, they are made whole.

### How we have it prefigured from Holy Scripture that Christ is the fountain of all merit, grace, and glory. Chapter IX.

This speech of **Christ** must be attended to, in which not without cause he preferred the sign of **Jonah** to other signs, because in it is included that for which **Christ** had chiefly come: namely, human redemption through the fullness of grace and merit. But let us enter into more secret mysteries: God had commanded this Jonah to preach to the erring Ninevites; and the Father commanded Christ to preach to and redeem the whole lost world. Jonah feared to undergo the burden imposed and busied himself to flee; and the Son of God began to fear and to be weary, and to procure a flight to the Father, saying: *Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me.* <margin>CHRIST.</margin> <note>original: "Pater, si possibile est, transeat a me calix iste"; quoting Matthew 26:39</note> Jonah fled even to the high sea and to the waters of mercy and grace which he sought for the Ninevites; Christ also fled to the waters to which he invited the thirsty, and through which he made us safe and purged us. A tempest arose in the sea from Jonah’s flight, or from the mercy obtained for the Ninevites, a contention having been made before the tribunal of divine justice, which did not wish to permit the crimes of the Ninevites to pass unpunished. In like manner, a storm was raised and excited in heaven and in the world, because that same tribunal would not allow the human race to be freed by the sole intercession of the Redeemer without a worthy penalty for their crimes. <margin>John <br/> Revelation</margin> It came to pass (says John) that there was a great battle in heaven, not only from the rebellion of the dragon and his followers, but also because they would not allow the human race to be redeemed, especially without a worthy punishment. Jonah offered himself to suffer for the Ninevites, saying: *Take me and throw me into the sea, and the sea will cease from you; for I know that on my account this great tempest has come.* <note>original: "Tollite me, & mittite in mare..."; quoting Jonah 1:12</note> But I do not refuse to be handed over to the sea to quiet these tumults raised against the sins of the Ninevites, for whose pardon I have prayed. In like manner, Christ, seeing the whole tribunal of God agitated and demanding vengeance for the evil deeds of the human race, and that justice could not stand if it were mitigated, the Son of God himself said: *Behold, here I am; throw me into this sea,* myself prepared to receive every punishment which is owed to all transgressors who are in this worldly sea.

And we thought him struck, beaten by God, and humbled, and did not think that he had voluntarily taken up those strikes for our redemption. But he was weakened because of our crimes or our transgressions, and he was crushed because of our iniquities. This is of the greatest importance: for from the Law, no one was justified except from a sin contracted through ignorance, or through a slip of the mind, and things of this sort, as we explained above. But from iniquity, which they call **עון** <term>Havon</term> <note>A Hebrew term for "iniquity," often implying a crookedness of character or intentional wrongdoing.</note>, and from transgression or rebellion, which they name **פשע** <term>Pissah</term> <note>Transliteration of the Hebrew 'Pesha,' referring to a revolt or a conscious breaking of a covenant.</note>, and from impiety, which they call **רשע** <term>Rashah</term> <note>Transliteration of 'Rasha,' signifying wickedness or the state of being guilty before God.</note>, there was no justification at all. Therefore David, having
<margin>David</margin>
committed adultery (which is called iniquity) and homicide (which is called impiety), knowing that such things were not purged by sacrifices, said: *For if you had desired sacrifice, I would have given it; certainly you will not be delighted with burnt offerings.* <note>Psalm 51:16</note> Hence Paul,
<margin>Paul</margin>
discussing this with the Romans, says: *No one will be justified by the law.* Such a person was ordered to be stoned or to be expiated by some kind of personal death. Coming from all these things, the Messiah has freed us. Therefore the prophet follows: *The discipline of our peace*—that is, the method of acquiring reconciliation with God—was upon him, and *by his bruises we are healed.* For all of us, like sheep, have gone astray; each one has turned aside into his own way. All were liable to sins, iniquities, and those guilts from which they could not be rescued. Therefore the Lord placed upon him the iniquities of us all. This work, although the physical senses resisted it, he nevertheless undertook voluntarily. Whence it follows: *He was offered because he himself willed it.* <note>Isaiah 53:7</note> For this reason he said to Peter, who was trying to rescue him from the hand of those capturing him: *The cup which the
<margin>CHRIST</margin>
Father has given me, do you not wish that I drink it?* And when Peter previously abhorred the name and the work of the cross, he said to him: *Get behind me, Satan, you are a scandal to me, for you do not savor the things of God, but the things of men.* Because he voluntarily undertook this work, he therefore did not open his mouth in his own defense, but like one mute...

He stood before Herod and Pilate, who sought to release him; hence it follows: 
*He shall be led like a sheep to the slaughter, and like a lamb before its shearer, he shall remain silent.* <note>Isaiah 53:7</note> He was indeed the Lamb taking away the sins of the world and all the crimes which could be expiated by no other sacrifice, sacrificed in the true Passover <note>original: "uero pascate" — the author links Christ’s death to the Jewish Passover, viewing it as the ultimate fulfillment of the ritual</note> and the passage to a better life. Because of the distress endured for us, and the judgment and sentence he sustained for us, he was accepted and glorified. And since he did those things which any ordinary man is unable to do, he is proved to be more than a man; hence the prophet adds: *Who shall declare his generation?* <note>original: "Generationem eius quis enarrabit?" — A traditional rhetorical question in theology emphasizing Christ's eternal, divine origin which defies human explanation</note> For he was cut off from the land—not of the dying, but of the living—he who had come to give us life. *For the iniquity of my people he was struck*, or a blow was inflicted on him, so that it might be the voice of the Eternal Father, or of the prophet narrating how we have struck him, so that it may be clearly understood that it is the Father's voice. It follows: *And he will give his burial to the wicked*, that is, by his death and burial he will grant the peoples the forgiveness of their sins and obtain pardon for them. *And he will acquire riches in his death*: for indeed he will be rich toward all who call upon that name which the Father gave him, because he was made obedient even unto death on the cross. *Nor did he commit iniquity, nor was deceit found in his mouth*, so that it would have been necessary for him to suffer for his own expiation; for our sake, therefore, the Lord willed to crush him. And because he knew that if he offered his soul for the sin of the people, he would see a *long-lived offspring* <note>original: "semen longæuū"</note>, he surrendered it willingly; hence he saw his offspring spread and multiplied more than that of Abraham, which, like the stars of heaven and the sand of the sea, was innumerable. For beyond the chosen and sealed princes, he begot a great multitude which no one could number. His offspring was also long-lived because his family lasts forever and possesses a perpetual kingdom, as it is said in the Psalm:

*His seed remains forever, and his throne is like the sun in my sight.* And again: *I will establish his seed for ever and ever, and his throne as the days of heaven.* It follows: *And the will of the Lord shall be directed in his hand*, or shall sprout, or shall prosper, as the literal truth holds:

It follows: *Therefore I will divide*, or share out for him many people, assigning them to him as a people to whom he may divide and bestow from his fullness. <margin>Paul
David</margin>
...he will divide the spoils, just as the Apostle says: *Despoiling the principalities and powers* <note>original: "Expolians principatus, & potestates" — a reference to Colossians 2:15, describing Christ’s victory over spiritual forces</note>. Concerning this, the Royal Prophet <note>David</note> also sings: *The beauty of the house shall divide the spoils* <note>Psalm 68:12</note>. He brought back these spoils from the victory held in his own death, for which reason it is added: *Because he delivered his soul unto death* <note>Isaiah 53:12</note>, specifically a death of shame; whence it follows: *And he was numbered with the wicked*, or the rebels. But he himself *bore the sins of many*, namely of those who desire the benefit of his redemption and who carry the cross while following him. Nor did he pray only for his crucifiers, but for all others, as Paul says: *In the days of his flesh, he offered up prayers with tears and a strong cry, and was heard for his reverence* <note>Hebrews 5:7</note>.

### Chapter XII.

<margin>The same
CHRIST.</margin>
**W**hile <note>The Latin begins with "Dum," often used to introduce a foundational premise</note> therefore he was our Messiah and Christ, through whom all things were previously made, and who is the *author and finisher of faith* <note>Hebrews 12:2</note>, filling all things with his divinity—existing as both the part and the whole, and in a certain way existing as all things in all people—he gives life to all members of the mystical body <note>term: mystical body — the "Corpus Mysticum," a theological concept where the Church is viewed as a living organism with Christ as the head and the faithful as the limbs</note>, just as the human soul does. He extends himself even to our artificial works and labors, as we can learn from his own name <note>Jesus/Christ</note>, which is full of sacraments, and from his titles—which were given not by chance, but according to events and fitting mysteries—so much so that his name alone is invoked by true worshipers. Furthermore, he took upon himself all our languors, infirmities, and debts, so that we, being set free, might be able to labor more readily. Rightly, then, he has become the one through whom we perform all things, as Paul says: *I can do all things in him who strengthens me* <note>Philippians 4:13</note>. And again: *The same God, who works all things in all* <note>1 Corinthians 12:6</note>. This is God in Christ Jesus, disposing all things, wherefore he himself says in open speech: *Without me you can do nothing* <note>John 15:5</note>; and *If anyone does not abide in me, he shall be cast out and wither, and they shall cast him into the fire, and he burns*. As God favors us, we shall disclose this more clearly at the end of this second volume. Therefore, we must run back to him, the giver of all good things and the true mediator, and through him we must entreat all things from the Father, so that by his nodding assent, he may give to us from the fullness of his riches. Enriched by these, we may appear honorably in the sight of so great a Prince, concerning whose dominion and kingdom we must now discourse.

# CHRIST IS THE TRUE LORD FORETOLD BY THE MOSAIC PROPHECIES. CHAPTER ONE.

<margin>Moses</margin>
In order to recount, at least in part, what the Holy Spirit foretold through the mouths of the prophets regarding the dominion and kingdom of our Christ, we must begin with Moses, the <term>Law-writer</term> <note>original: "Legigraphus"; a Greek-derived Latin term for Moses as the author of the Divine Law</note>. For when he speaks of the birth of man, he seems to record his production twice: First, he relates that He created them male and female, in His own image and likeness. Afterward, as if he had said nothing about man, he says in the following section: "And there was no man to work the earth," wherefore "the Lord God formed man from the slime of the earth," or the dust of the ground, "and breathed into his face the breath of life." One must not think that such a great man—most learned in all wisdom, full of God, and filled with the Holy Spirit—was struck by such dullness that, forgetful of what he had said just a moment before, he would repeat the formation of him whom he had already declared to be made in the likeness and image of God and appointed as the Lord of all things. By the same reasoning, after he had related that male and female were produced, he would not immediately forget what he had said and add: "And for the man there was not found a helper like himself," or one who might stand before him, as the literal truth holds. For who could ascribe such mental laziness to so great a man—that he would repeat the same thing in vain—when he did not interpose even a superfluous jot in his description? Therefore, to remove this apparent error from a man full of God and from the sacred utterances, we reveal from the most sacred storehouses (as those most skilled in these matters <note>This likely refers to mystical or Kabbalistic commentators who reconciled the two creation stories in Genesis</note> affirm) that Moses first described the Messiah and the production of His mother. Of these, Christ is the one with the true image of God and the firstborn of all, as <margin>Paul</margin> Paul says: *Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature.* And He Himself was made male, and she herself female, in the divine mind first, and before, and above all others. To them He also subjected all things, saying: *Rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of the air, the beasts of the earth, and all living things that move upon the earth.* Singing of this, the divine <margin>David</margin> <term>Harp-player</term> <note>original: "Citharœdus"; a common epithet for King David as the author of the Psalms</note> says: *You have crowned him with glory and honor, and have set him over the works of your hands; you have subjected all things under his feet: sheep and oxen, all of them, and moreover the beasts of the field, the birds of the air, and the fish of the sea, and whatever walks through the paths of the sea.* And that this is sung there concerning Christ, <margin>Paul</margin> Paul—the unlocker of secrets—explains in open discourse to the Corinthians and the Hebrews, saying those things were foretold of Christ; and coming to that word, *You have subjected all things under his feet,* he says: *In that he subjected all things, he left nothing not subject, except him who subjected all things,* to whom that son was subject; <margin>The same</margin> Whom (as he...

Jacob is also introduced by Moses prophesying to his son Judah, saying: "The scepter shall not be taken away from Judah, nor a leader from his thigh, nor a lawgiver from the midst of his feet" (as the literal truth holds) "until he comes who is to be sent: and he shall be the expectation of the nations." <margin>Onkelos</margin>
"until **Shiloh** comes." <note>original: "שילה"</note> This term, the <term>Targum Onkelos</term> <note>An ancient and authoritative Aramaic translation and commentary on the Hebrew Bible</note>—most celebrated among the Hebrews—renders in Chaldaic as **Messiah** <note>original: "משיחא"</note>. <note>This is a literal English translation of the Aramaic text provided in the manuscript.</note> This is also supported

<margin>David Kimhi</margin>
by <term>David Kimhi</term> <note>A famous medieval rabbi and grammarian, often referred to by the acronym "Radak"</note>, who brings forward many arguments to prove that by "Shiloh," the Messiah must be understood. Nor should one listen to more recent Hebrews, who interpret those words variously and always erroneously to defend their own stubbornness.

<margin>Nebuchadnezzar</margin>
For some say that this "Shiloh" was Nebuchadnezzar, the King of Babylon, sent by God to punish the sins of the Jewish people; he put an end to the kingdom of Judah when King Zedekiah was led away as a captive to Babylon, and the city and temple were devastated—so much so that there was never again a king in Jerusalem, nor from the house of Judah. And they say that this Nebuchadnezzar was the "expectation of the nations" because under him the dominion and empire of the nations were expanded. But these people should really be laughed at and hissed off the stage rather than listened to. This is because "Shiloh" does not mean "sent," nor was Nebuchadnezzar the expectation of the nations, nor were any nations gathered to him other than the Chaldeans, Persians, and Medes, who are but a small part compared to other nations. Nor did the Judean scepter fail entirely under Nebuchadnezzar, because when the people were brought back from captivity, there were many leaders in that tribe. Others say that this took place in Saul, who was from the tribe of Benjamin and was anointed king in Shiloh; for then the glory of the kingdom and the scepter of Judah passed to the tribe of Benjamin. This is no less ridiculous than the first claim, since the scepter of the kingdom was not taken away from Judah—for God's decree that this tribe should have a king had not yet been put into execution, even though it had always been the royal tribe by divine sanction. Therefore (as the wiser Hebrews say), Jacob believed the promise made by Judah for the return of Benjamin more than he believed the other ten sons who stood as sureties for him, as we read in the book of Genesis. Therefore, this royal scepter was granted to the tribe of Judah from the beginning...

<header>OF THE SECOND CANTICLE</header>

[The kingdom was] granted by God, permitted to be assigned to the tribe of Benjamin for a brief time, and then immediately restored to the tribe of Judah in the person of David while Saul was still living. And the kingdom endured in that family for fourteen generations, until the Babylonian captivity. After that time, there were still leaders from the tribe of Judah, such as Zerubbabel <note>The grandson of King Jehoiachin who led the first group of Jews back from Babylonian exile</note> and those who followed him. Nor was Saul anointed in Shiloh, but in Kiriath-Jearim (as some say) or in the land of Zuph, as is held in the first book of Kings <note>Known as 1 Samuel in modern Bibles</note>.

I have also found those in our own time who impudently assert that the oracle found its fulfillment in Jeroboam; for at that time ten tribes were taken away from the Judean scepter and given to Jeroboam himself, who was of the tribe of Ephraim, just as Ahijah the Shilonite had prophesied to him. They say, therefore: "Until Shiloh comes," meaning Ahijah of Shiloh. This interpretation cannot stand at all, because the kingdom was not then taken away from the tribe of Judah, but only diminished, with the kingdom remaining under Rehoboam and his descendants for another twelve generations. Afterward, there were very many leaders in whom the scepter still persisted. For <term>שבט</term> (*shebet*), <note>original: "shebet" — a Hebrew word meaning a rod, staff, or scepter, symbolizing authority</note> which we have translated as "scepter," can refer to Leaders as much as to Kings, as is found in the
<margin>Judges 5</margin>
Book of Judges, where it is said: "From Machir the princes came down, and from Zebulun those who lead the army to war." Or, as the Hebrew truth has it: "And from Zebulun he who draws or leads with the scribe's rod." Here the Hebrew uses the word <term>שבט</term> (*shebet*), which in neither Latin nor Hebrew can stand for a "royal scepter," since there was never a kingdom in the tribe of Zebulun, but certainly there was leadership and the "scepter" of a leader.

Indeed, there were leaders in the tribe of Judah even after the Babylonian captivity—great legislators, interpreters, or doctors of the law—until the time of Herod of Ascalon <note>Herod the Great</note>, in the thirty-first year of whose reign our Christ was born. Nor did any foreigner rule over them before him, once the scepter had been given to the people and to that tribe of Judah, nor in the region assigned to them. At that time, therefore, the scepter was taken away from that tribe—a scepter that had fallen silent during the Babylonian captivity. It was not taken away unfavorably, but most happily by the Messiah; for it was changed for the better, from a temporal and earthly scepter into one that is perpetual and heavenly. And this was done through the Messiah himself, who was of that same tribe and the true King of kings and Lord of lords, although his kingdom did not appear in this world. Indeed, so that he might devote himself to the heavenly kingdom, having been made the true exemplar for all, he remained free from this temporal rule; although he held full dominion over it, as he himself testified, saying: "All power is given to me in heaven and on earth." <note>Matthew 28:18</note> Even while acting in human affairs, he used this power as he pleased, commanding the sea and the winds, multiplying loaves and fishes, driving out various infirmities and afflictions, but most especially despoiling the prince of this world <note>Satan</note> and casting him out. But he dominates much more happily now in that kingdom, even though he has fixed his seat in the heavens; for a name has been given to him at which every knee shall bow, of those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth. This, then, is the Messiah, the Christ, anointed above all as the true King, Priest, and Prophet, unto whom all nations are gathered, so that...

<header>SEVENTH TONE</header>

It is held in the text: **and to him shall be the gathering of the peoples** <note>Hebrew: *velo yikehat amim*</note>: which is interpreted word-for-word as: *And to him the nations, or the people, shall be gathered.* In place of this, our translation <note>The Latin Vulgate</note> has: **And he shall be the expectation of the nations.** For the nations were never gathered to any ruler of the Israelite family so as to obey his authority, except for Christ: to whom the whole world has clung, and from every nation that is under heaven. For he draws all to himself by his own power, even his enemies, just as the oracle had said earlier: **Thy hand shall be in the necks of thy enemies, and thy father’s children shall adore thee.** This refers to the Heavenly Father, who rules over all and is called the Father of all. Therefore, he extends his dominion and kingdom even to foreigners, just as the divine 
<margin>David</margin> 
Harp-player <note>A poetic title for King David as the author of the Psalms</note> sings: *Judah is my king*, that is, <term>Adonai</term> <note>Lord</note>, or the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter divine name of God, YHWH</note> made human, is my king. For **Judah** <note>Hebrew: יהודה (Yehudah)</note> is written in Hebrew with the four letters of the great four-letter name, with a **ד** (*dalet*) interposed, which signifies "four," that is, the squareness of the bodily mass <note>The author is using Christian Kabbalah to argue that the name of Judah contains the name of God (YHWH) plus the letter Dalet, representing the physical world or the four elements, symbolizing the Incarnation</note>. The prophet continues: **Moab is the pot of my hope**, meaning it must be purged in the furnace, or fire, and in the pot of testing, so that it may be an example to all who are converted. **Into Edom will I extend my shoe**, that is, the humanity with which the Edomite people are shod and clothed, along with the entire human race that was stripped and made naked in the sin of the <term>protoplast</term> <note>Adam, the first-formed human</note>, and also in those sins which each individual commits. And because even the outside nations are redeemed by him, it follows: **The foreigners are made subject to me.** Thus the royal staff, which was confined to the tribe of Judah, was so expanded in Christ that it was extended not only to that family and the house of Israel, but unto all things, since all things are subject to Christ. Then that which follows was fulfilled: 
<margin>Jerome</margin> 
**He shall tie his foal to the vine, and his ass’s colt to the branches**, or shoots, **of the vine, O my son.** By the "foal" (as <note>Saint</note> Jerome rightly feels), the Gentile people are understood, who are new in the faith and a son of mercy and grace; they are tied to that vine which says: *I am the vine.* 
<margin>CHRIST</margin> 
The "ass" is indeed Mother Church, whose son is both the Gentile and the Israelite people; but the former is the "new one" and the "foal," while the latter is now long-lived. These are perhaps indicated by the two sons, one of whom, having received his portion from the father, squandered it and consumed it in a far-off region, having become in a way a stranger to his father <note>An allusion to the Parable of the Prodigal Son</note>. Therefore, not without a mystery, he tied the Mother Church of these people (signified by the ass) to the shoots or the branches of the vine, to which she herself said in support: *And you are the branches staying in me.* For he commended and subjected the Church to the Apostles and their successors, so much so that she is bound by their institutes and judgments. And because an idolatrous bride, polluted by other alliances, ought not to be joined to Christ, a most pure and holy man, it follows: **He shall wash his garment in wine, and his clothing in the blood of grapes.** This "garment" is either that made from the skin of the Lamb, dyed and cleansed by his blood, with which he covered the nakedness of the entire human race; or it is the Gentile people, and everyone who, recognizing the benefit of redemption, has clung to Christ, covering the shame brought upon Christ in his passion, lest he should seem to have endured so many mockeries in vain.

The author uses Hebrew etymology and the imagery of the vine and the foal to explain the transition from the tribal scepter to the spiritual authority of the Church.</summary>

### Chapter II.

<margin>David</margin>
Let us run through a few examples of many concerning what other Seers predicted about this dominion and the kingdom given to our Jesus. For David, speaking in his person in the second Psalm, says: **The Lord said to me: You are my son, today I have begotten you.** In the Hebrew <margin>Au. etc.</margin> this is held as: <term>היום ילדתיך</term> <note>original: *haiom ieliditica*</note> "today I have begotten you." By this word *haiom* ("today"), eternity is understood—a state without any determined time—as is well interpreted by the author of the book called *The Words of Beauty* <note>original: *Eloquia pulchritudinis*; likely a reference to the Hebrew work *Imre Shefer* by Naphtali Herz Treves, or a similar kabbalistic commentary</note>. Therefore, regarding him who was begotten from eternity and born in time according to the flesh, he says: **Ask of me, and I will give you the nations for your inheritance, and the ends of the earth for your possession.** That is: *Ask by carrying out the work I have established*, so that you may have legitimate dominion in all the ends of the earth. 

This dominion he has held and continues to hold, even though the <margin>Paul</margin> Muhammadan division <note>original: *discissio mahumetica*; referring to the rise of Islam as a historical-theological "schism" or "tearing away"</note> was permitted by divine dispensation, not without order and mystery. Much could be said of this, but I will only bring forward what Paul, who shared in God’s secrets, wrote by way of prophecy to the Thessalonians: **Let no one terrify you or lead you astray by word or by letter, as if the day of the Lord were at hand: for it shall not come**—that is, showing the authority of his empire upon the seat of his majesty—**unless the rebellion comes first.** This truly and greatly occurred through Muhammad. **And the man of sin shall also be revealed, the son of perdition, who will oppose and be exalted above everything that is called God.** Hence he is called the Antichrist and the "Anti-god"—that is, against Christ and God. But the Lord Jesus shall kill him with the breath of his mouth, and shall restore those things that were torn apart by the Muhammadan beast. Then he shall rule all things with **an iron rod**—that is, an insuperable and utterly invincible power—**and he shall break them like a potter’s vessel**, namely the beast with its sect, and the son of iniquity with his <margin>David</margin> father, the devil, who holds the empire of death; for then death, the enemy, shall be destroyed. 

In another Psalm the same prophet says: **He shall call upon me: You are my Father, and the strength** (or the rock, or the refuge) **of my salvation. And I will make him my firstborn, high above the kings of the earth.** Thus he is rightly called <margin>John</margin> (as John says) **King of kings, and Lord of lords, and Prince of the king-**

### Chapter III. Why Christ is not said to reign in the house of Abraham, although the promise was first made to him.

Abraham, beyond all doubt, was called the father of the chosen family and the father of faith, being the leader (as we are taught in the Gospel) of the "bosom" into which all the elect flowed <note>A reference to "Abraham's Bosom," a place of comfort for the righteous dead mentioned in Luke 16:22</note>. Nevertheless, the heavenly oracle did not say, when announcing the conception of the Redeemer: "He shall reign in the house of Abraham," but "He shall reign in the house of Jacob." This, I believe, was because it was said to Abraham: **Cast out the bondwoman and her son.** <note>Genesis 21:10; referring to Hagar and Ishmael</note> In this, Abraham carries the image of a great and universal father who has both good and bad sons, the just and the unjust, upon whom he rains and makes his sun to rise. Therefore, not without mystery was he called Abraham instead of Abram, that is, "Father of many and mixed nations." <note>The author provides a popular etymology for the name change from Abram to Abraham in Genesis 17:5</note> He also holds the image of a father in his offspring and progeny: for he had Isaac from a legitimate marriage and Ishmael from an illegitimate one. But—alas—where am I entering? What will be the legitimate and illegitimate marriage of the paternal and divine mind, so that Abraham may hold its likeness there? It was indeed legi-

# OF THE SECOND SONG

...the devil, and by what means he himself—as well as the delight that surrounded his production and preservation—was cast out. Since in God there is neither external delight, nor is anything cast out as if it were rejected by the Highest Good, we can respond sufficiently by declaring that although the best God is happy without any external good and lacks none of our goods—indeed, He bestows all those things upon us—nevertheless, <margin>Solomon</margin> Solomon, acting in His person, sings in the Proverbs: *And my delights were to be with the sons of men.* <note>Proverbs 8:31. The author uses this to show that God chooses to delight in creation, even if He does not "need" it for His own happiness.</note> And if He takes pleasure in human minds, it is fitting that He also takes pleasure in higher or angelic beings.

He also delights in each individual creature He produced, as He had said shortly before: *And I was delighted day by day*, that is, in every single form appearing in my creatures, whatever it might be. For it is characteristic of any craftsman to take delight in the works of his own hands, in which he senses and perceives an image or likeness of himself; this nature itself brings a wonderful delight to the craftsman. Nor is there to me any more elegant reason why God loves His creatures so much, except that He senses something of His own in the work and beholds His own image or <term>footprint|Latin: *vestigium*. In medieval theology, a 'trace' of God found in all created things, whereas 'image' (imago) is reserved for rational beings.</term>. This delight does not come from the external work but flows from the Craftsman Himself along with the idea and form of things, all of which are drawn from the heavenly pattern. When this delight passes into creatures, it deservedly receives the name of a "handmaid." <note>An allegory for Hagar, the servant-mother of Ishmael, representing the created order that is secondary to the divine Son.</note> He therefore drives her from His royal house along with her son when someone is found to be unclean or a rebel and unworthy of such a banquet and kingdom. 

Thus, that wicked and rebellious one was first expelled from that kingdom with his attendants because he wished to be made the heir and to oppress the legitimate son. This "bastard"—that is, the one born from a secondary, complacent delight—stood in the father's kingdom for as long as he respected the legitimate son. But as soon as he rose up against him, he was cast out together with those clinging to him. Then the image of the Father was taken from him, along with the resulting delight. For from a most beautiful Angel, he became a horrid serpent, and from a domestic friend, he became a most bitter enemy. In this kingdom, not yet pacified, the eternal Father did not wish the Son to reign—who is called the *Prince of Peace*—since it was necessary that first *his enemies be placed as a footstool for his feet*, <note>A reference to Psalm 110:1, often cited in the New Testament to explain why Christ's total rule is not yet visible.</note> as the heavenly oracle says. Therefore, it was not said: *He shall reign in the house of Abraham.* 

Why does He not even reign in the house of Isaac, to whom the promise was made for the second time?

->### Chapter IV<-

Here, Esau represents the "animal" or "earthly" nature that exists alongside the spiritual.</note> This one was given into the service of his younger brother, supplanted by him, and despoiled of his birthright; he was made a servant for as long as he wrongly persecuted his brother. These things, like the rest, were described with great mystery as a figure of better things. For he also bears the image of the Craftsman, who created man in two ways: first the animal man...

<margin>Paul</margin> ...hates; then the spiritual man, whom he loves, as Paul says: *First that which is soulish <note>original: "animale." The forefather commands that the elder serve the younger, when he says to the "better man": *Your appetite shall be under you.* <note>A reference to the control of physical impulses.</note> And he hates the elder so long as he remains rebellious against the brother to whom he ought to be subject.

<margin>Christ</margin> Christ does not admit a person into friendship, nor does He reign within them, unless they submit themselves to the younger-born <note>The "younger" here represents the spirit/Jacob, while the "older" represents the flesh/Esau.</note>, just as He said while debating with Pilate: *My kingdom is not of this world*, in which the "animal man" prevails—namely Esau, who is also called Edom, meaning "red" or "bloody." Indeed, He openly admits the hostilities that exist between them when He says: *If the world hates you, know that it hated me before you.* <margin>The Same [Christ]</margin> <margin>James, John</margin> Taught by Him, His two closest disciples, James and John, agree in asserting this: *Whoever wishes to be a friend of this world is constituted an enemy of God.*

<margin>Paul</margin> And so that it may be clearly understood of whom he speaks, Paul, after discussing much regarding the "animal" and "spiritual" man, adds: *Flesh and blood cannot possess the kingdom of God*, unless (that is) they are changed for the better, into the nature of the spirit. He continues, saying: *This corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality.* Nor is it without mystery that the younger <term>supplants|Latin: *supplantat*. A play on the name "Jacob," which traditionally means "supplanter" or "he who trips up."</term> and subdues the elder, as <margin>The Same [Paul]</margin> Paul says: *I chastise my body and bring it into servitude.* Therefore, the younger takes away the birthright—namely the dignity of preeminence and the worship of God—which belongs to the spiritual man, not the animal man.

He also snatches away the blessing, not without mystery: for he is blessed with the true blessing who, being devoted to God, embraces his neighbor with the charity he owes him. We have this from our true Forefather, who says to such pious and kind people: <margin>Christ</margin> *Come, you blessed of my Father, possess the kingdom prepared for you.* He snatches this blessing through the persuasion of his mother Rebecca—that is, the Church—who teaches how to sanctify a man so that he may be capable of that great blessing, which the <margin>Isaac</margin> Father Isaac mystically hints at when he says: *May God give to you of the dew of heaven, and of the fatness of the earth, an abundance of grain, wine, and oil. Let peoples serve you, and tribes adore you. Be lord of your brothers, and let the sons of your mother bow down before you. Cursed be he who curses you, and let him who blesses you be filled with blessings.*

The first portion of this blessing is "of the dew of heaven"—specifically that supramundane dew designated by <term>Hermon|Latin: *hermon*. Traditionally interpreted in some medieval etymologies as "anathema" or "destruction," which the author links to the banishing of grief.</term>, which is called the "banishment of sorrow." <margin>Dew</margin> "Dew" is a distillation from heaven, denoting the sprinkling of divine grace, or the Holy Spirit, or whatever good flows from that super-celestial homeland where all sorrow and pain is banished. This is the first portion of the blessing given to a true Israelite. He also adds "of the fatness of the earth"—though not indeed *all* fatness...

<margin>Plotinus</margin>
It is necessary that the eye beholding it be beautiful, as **Plotinus** <note>Plotinus (c. 204–270 AD) was a major Greek-speaking philosopher of the Neoplatonic school. Therefore, those ancient fathers decreed that no one should be admitted to the solitary and contemplative life unless they had been exercised for eighteen or twenty years in works of charity and the service of the monastery. For this is the custom of the homeland and the family dedicated to God: that a man, purged through works of penance and labor, may ascend to the sweet contemplation of divine things. For this he serves for repeated seven-year periods, so that the two-fold man <note>Likely referring to the dual nature of man (body and soul) or the dual life (active and contemplative).</note>, well-purified and initiated, may be free for God. 

For the <term>septenary number</term> <note>The number seven.</note> is "critical," purifying, and releasing. It is "critical" <note>original: "creticus." In ancient medicine, "critical days" (dies critici) were those on which a disease was expected to reach a turning point or "crisis."</note> because in it, changes and renewals commonly occur. For it is discerned in the seventh hour whether an infant will live; after seven days, it casts off the remains of the umbilical cord; after twice seven days, its eyes begin to move toward the light; and after seven times seven days, it now freely turns its pupils and entire face toward every object of fear or sight. After seven months, the teeth begin to emerge from the jaws; after twice seven months, it sits without fear of falling; after thrice seven months, its sound breaks forth into words; after four times seven months, it not only stands firmly but walks; after five times seven months, it begins to lose its taste for the nurse’s milk. In the seventh year, the teeth are changed for those more suitable, and in that same year, the perfection of speech is fully completed. When the second week of years <note>The age of 14.</note> is finished, it enters puberty, and the power of generation begins to move.

In the third week <note>The age of 21.</note>, it shows the flowers and downy hair of youth. In the fourth <note>The age of 28.</note>, the increments of height are finalized. In the fifth <note>The age of 35.</note>, youthful perfection is completed. In the sixth <note>The age of 42.</note>, the strengths previously gathered are preserved. But let us return to the two wives, each of whom has her own handmaid. These lawful wives are the **active life** and the **contemplative life**, in which the two powers of Jacob—namely, the **intellect** and the **will**—delight together. Or (as the <margin>Academics</margin> Academics <note>Followers of the Platonic school of philosophy.</note> teach), that higher portion of the intellect, which some call <term>synderesis</term> <note>In medieval theology, the innate spark of conscience that knows the basic principles of right and wrong.</note>, and the rational and discursive portion; the latter serves the active life, while the former serves the contemplative.

But the mystery is to be wondered at: how each of them offers her own handmaid. Certainly, that higher and contemplative portion has a handmaid, through whom it may delight in contemplating these created and lower things, and through these visible things, it may ascend to the invisible Creator. This is **discursive reason** joined to the senses, through which it perceives sensible things. Our Jacob is joined to this handmaid when, through the sight of these lower things, he hunts for the greatness of the Architect. But he is joined to **Rachel** when he gazes upon and contemplates the very beginning of things and the fountain of all goods in the light emanating from Him with the eye of the mind.

<margin>The lower portion</margin>
The lower portion—that is, the will or the operative virtue—also has its handmaid, namely, **delight** in performing tasks. If Jacob (the spiritual man directing all things toward God) is joined to this delight or co-delighting virtue, he himself brings forth good fruits worthy of eternal life. He is joined to **Leah** when he acts immediately for the sake of God. But let us also observe the names of the handmaids, if they are fitting: Rachel's handmaid is **Bilah** <note>original: "Bala." Jacob's concubine and Rachel's handmaid.</note>, which is said to mean "swallowed up" or "aged." ### Of the fruits of this house, in which Christ reigns. Chapter VI.

But let us see what the fruits are that Jacob received from these wives and handmaids. First, it is not without mystery <note>A common theological phrase suggesting a hidden, sacred meaning.</note> that he had more children by Leah <note>original: "Lia"</note> than by Rachel, because we expect more fruits from the **active life** <note>The "active life" refers to practical service, charity, and labor in the world.</note> than from the **contemplative life** <note>The "contemplative life" refers to prayer, meditation, and direct focus on God.</note>, and more timely ones, even though we expect more lovable ones from the contemplative life. Hence, even though the choice of Mary is commended by the Savior because it is the "best part," <note>Referring to the story of Martha and Mary in Luke 10:38–42.</note> yet the concern of Martha is not blamed, although she feels many labors and much disturbance. That part is also the best which presupposes the merit of the active life and strives to climb higher. Therefore, the first son of Rachel is called Joseph, which means "increase" <note>original: "augmentum"</note> regarding all things that were acquired in the prior life. From this it is also declared why the latest fruits are from Rachel: because, of course, all the fruits of the active life, through which we are prepared for the contemplative life, are presupposed. 

This also must not be overlooked: that Jacob does not commit adultery with the handmaids, nor do the wives take it poorly; rather, they offer the handmaids of their own accord. This is because if a person takes delight in speculating upon and handling created things, as long as they direct all things toward God, they do not sin, but rather earn merit. Nor does either portion of the soul—which seeks God immediately—take it poorly; they voluntarily offer to the man the delight of created things as well, provided that they themselves <margin>Rachel</margin> receive the offspring conceived from the handmaids. Therefore Rachel said: *I have a handmaid Bilhah <note>original: "Bala"</note>; go into her, that she may bear upon my knees, and I may have sons from her.* Her sister <note>Leah.</note>, being moved by emulation, did the same. 

But coming to the particular sons, let us begin from the birth with which the spiritual man begins: because fruit is produced far more easily through the active life than through the contemplative life. From her <note>Leah/The Active Life.</note>, therefore, is first born Reuben, afterward Simeon, Levi, and Judah. Reuben, who is interpreted as "seeing through a medium," <note>original: "uidens per medium"</note> signifies a **holy intention**, which directs all things by a straight path toward God, so that it turns neither to the right nor to the left. <margin>CHRIST</margin> And this intention ought to be the "first-born" if we desire to produce sons and fruits worthy of eternal life; which the Savior warns with an uplifted voice, saying: 
> If your eye is simple, your whole body will be bright; you will have 
> no part of darkness, but like a lamp of brilliance it will illuminate you, 
> looking through a true medium at the object toward which we strive. 
For this "eye" (as all agree) signifies intention. After intention in performing deeds and observing precepts follows obedience toward the one commanding, so that all things are carried out at his nod. Hence, second is born...

**Simeon**, who is interpreted as "hearing" and "obeying." **Levi** <note>original: "Leui"</note> follows, who is said to mean "joined," "added," or "applied": because once a person has a right intention along with a readiness to obey, it remains for him to "apply" his hands to the work. And because in all things that we do, we ought to praise God by calling upon His name, **Judah** <note>original: "Iehuda"</note> is born after these, whose name is said by our people to mean "praise" or "confession." But seeing the **contemplative life** <note>represented by Rachel</note>, or that higher portion of the soul, envied the hasty and fertile birth of her sister <note>Leah, representing the active life</note> with a most holy zeal. And since she did not yet feel herself perfect enough to give birth—because, not yet being fully purified, she cannot yet fix her eye upon God—she offers her handmaid <note>Bilhah</note>, that is, the **contemplation of created things**. Through this contemplation of the created world, one arrives at the invisible things of God; thus she conceives and gives birth to **Dan**, that is, the "judgment" or "estimation" of the greatness of divine things based on these created things which she contemplates; or, the judgment by which she most subtly condemns and purifies herself so that she may be able to stretch toward God directly. Immediately after him, **Naphtali** <note>original: "Nephtalim"</note> is conceived and born, which is called the "broadening of the heart": because from the greatness of created things contemplated by a purified mind, the heart is broadened so that it may run toward God. The sister <note>Leah</note>, emulating this, also offers her own handmaid <note>Zilpah</note>, which signifies a certain "delight" in handling affairs; this acts like a spur and a certain stimulus that makes our mind diligent in accumulating merits. From this, **Gad** is later well-produced, who is "girded"—namely, for the prey and the heap of merits. Enriched by these merits and somewhat content, the soul considers herself blessed; hence she afterwards receives **Asher** <note>original: "Asser"</note>, who signifies "blessedness." Wherefore, still joyful and pleasant, she is encouraged toward further offspring, receiving a pair again, **Issachar** and **Zebulun**: of whom one is interpreted as "mindful of the Lord" and the other as "a dwelling place of strength." This indicates that the **active life**, once perfected, enriched with merits, and its work completed, arranges the house of the mind with the most beautiful ornament so that it may be able to receive the heavenly guest, of whom it is always mindful, so that it may be free for God Himself through contemplation. Therefore, our **Jacob** <note>original: "Iahacob"</note>, resting from the works produced and received from Leah—which pertain to the active life itself and to the preliminaries of the contemplative—it remains for him to devote himself only to **Rachel** and to perfect contemplation. From her he first receives **Joseph**, who is called "increase"—namely, the increase of all the works and merits which he received from Leah and from both handmaids. For this reason (unless I am mistaken), this is the "best part," <note>A reference to the "better part" chosen by Mary in the Gospels.</note> not only because it is safer and more pleasant, but because it presupposes every merit of the active life and seeks an increase. Therefore, he loves this birth more than the others, because it is enriched by all, and because he fathered him in the best sort of stillness. Nor is it without mystery that Rachel was prepared for this birth by the **mandrakes** <note>original: "mandragoris"</note> which Leah’s firstborn, **Reuben**, had given to her. We declared above that Reuben signifies "intention"; for the same intention that was a precursor in the fruits of the operative <note>active</note> life is also sought in the progress and fruitfulness of the contemplative life, so that in both places, the soul may look into that very thing through a straight and middle line.

With a well-affirmed intention, one comes to the offspring of the **contemplative life**, namely **Joseph** and **Benjamin**, in whose tribes and families alone the houses of God were located—and not without a mystery <note>The author uses "mystery" in the sense of a hidden spiritual truth (mystērion).</note>. His name is interpreted as "son of the right hand," signifying no one other than Him who sits at the right hand of God, **Jesus Christ our Redeemer**. All perfect people ought to father Him in their minds and in their innermost being; after Him, as if He were the final offspring, they should cease to give birth.

# VOLUME SEVEN

...He will judge those on the outside, he who holds primacy over all and is called—not without merit—King of kings and Lord of lords. <note>original: "Rex regum, & Dominus dominantium"</note> Nor should anyone persuade himself that this judgment and this throne were given to the Apostles out of the mere whim of the Prince; for even though His will is the primary rule of all things and can stand in place of reason, nevertheless, as the most just Prince—indeed, the very fountain of all-encompassing rectitude—He disposes all things in an orderly fashion. He could indeed grant paradise without merits; nonetheless, He decreed that soldiers should be rewarded according to the noble deeds of each. He could likewise forgive the injury brought upon Him by enemies and deserters without any penance; yet He commanded that everyone who sins be subject to the law of penance, according to the gravity of the offense. He was also able to grant the empire and dominion of the universe to the Son by a mere nod; yet He did not do so, but rather ordained that the Son should acquire dominion for Himself by hereditary and martial right, <note>Christ's "martial right" refers to his victory over death and the devil.</note> and that He should possess it most peacefully once the enemies had been defeated and put to flight. For indeed, He is the firstborn of Him who fashioned all things. 

Hence, the Magnanimous Emperor challenged that most cruel tyrant of the human race and prince of the world to a single combat, whom He also overthrew with a successful victory. <note>original: "fœlici marte," literally "with happy Mars," a classical idiom for a fortunate war or military success.</note> With the blood flowing from His own noble wounds, He washed away all human filth, and restored those unjustly oppressed by the most wicked tyrant to their

A part of this glory is the dominion and sovereignty over all things. 

In a similar way, He led His chosen princes, whom He sent into the whole world to preach the gospel to every creature, and He assigned to each a portion of the world's family. Thus, by preaching and teaching to them, and even spending their blood as a testimony to their doctrine, they might deservedly preside over the tribe, or family, or nation which they acquired, as if over children and those who were in some way redeemed (though by the power of the Supreme Redeemer). And these are the true twelve tribes over which the Emperor and Redeemer of the universe promised presidency and judgment to the Apostles. 

Those twelve Israelite tribes were a small image and figure of these; and each family was distributed by the number twelve. The Apostolic family was so distributed so that it might follow the twelve parts of the globe, corresponding to the twelve signs <note>The twelve signs of the Zodiac.</note> in the proper order. The Israelite family, however, was meant to prefigure the twelvefold family of the Church by that same number. And both were most excellently divided by that "first increasing" twelve-fold number, just as all increasing things (as we touched on above) are numbered. For that symbolic nation grew to an immense size in a very short time, so much so that it first filled Egypt, and afterward that Promised Land, which bore the likeness of the Holy Church. The twelve tribes taught and acquired by the Apostles also grew, so that in a short time they filled the whole world with believers. That mystery of sacred things must also be considered, namely that the number twelve is born from four triangles, or from three groups of four, and is divided like a solid body into four corners: which is found to be observed in both these families <note>The Tribes of Israel and the Apostles</note> and in the heaven of the stars.
