since in many places of Holy Scripture they are declared exempt from them, just as Ptolemy admits in his *Centiloquium* <note>original: "Fructu"; referring to the *Karpos* or *Centiloquium*, a collection of 100 astrological aphorisms traditionally attributed to the famous astronomer Claudius Ptolemy</note>. Rather, it was so that they might correspond to the supermundane <note>Beyond the physical world or the visible heavens</note> heaven, by which we are all chiefly directed and to which we must all be conformed. In this heaven there are also four quarters, as 
<margin>Isaiah</margin>
we are taught by Scripture: The East, of which Isaiah says: *His name is the East* <note>original: "Nomen eius oriens"; likely a reference to Zechariah 6:12 or Isaiah 41:2, identifying the Messiah with the rising sun</note>; and again: *Calling a righteous man from the east.* For from there comes the Messiah. The South, of which Habakkuk says: *God shall come from the South.* Nor do the prophets disagree, since He comes from both places, as is known to those who understand these names and the correspondence of the lower world with the Archetype <note>The original divine pattern from which the world was made</note>. The West, for which the Hebrews commonly use the word "sea," indicates those supreme waters with which Christ comes, 
<margin>John</margin>
as John says: *This is Jesus, who came by water and blood.* For this should not be understood as elemental water, but as super-celestial and spiritual water. The North is the rectitude of justice, from which all evil is spread and manifested <note>A reference to Jeremiah 1:14: "Out of the north an evil shall break forth"</note>; it is first discerned by a righteous judge and afterwards punished. These supermundane aspects are prior to those named by the course of the sun; and the latter receive all their force and strength from the former. According to these aspects, by a great mystery, the tribes were commanded to camp—not only those of that typical family <note>The historical tribes of Israel as a "type" or foreshadowing</note>, but the true and militant church under Christ the Prince, as we shall say shortly.

<margin>Image</margin>
The earthy <term>trigon: a grouping of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element, also known as a triplicity</term> is southern and stretches from the south toward the east; its images are Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn. Its Lords are Venus, Mercury, and Saturn. To Taurus, along with Venus, are subjected the Cyclades, the coastal regions of Asia Minor, Cyprus, Parthia, Media, and Persia. To Virgo, along with Mercury: Greece, Achaia, Crete, Babylon, Mesopotamia, Assyria, and Elam (from whence come the Elamites). But to Capricorn and Saturn: Macedonia, Thrace, Illyria, India, Ariana, Gordiana—many of which regions are in Asia Minor. The third trigon is watery and western, extended from the west toward the south; its images are Pisces, Cancer, and Scorpio. Its Lords are Jupiter, the Moon, and Mars. To Pisces, along with Jupiter, are subjected Lycia, Lydia, Cilicia, Pamphylia, Paphlagonia, Nasamonia, and Garamantica. To Cancer and the Moon: Bithynia, Phrygia, Colchis, Numidia, Africa, Carthage, and all of Carchedonia <note>A regional name for the territory surrounding Carthage</note>. To Scorpio and Mars: Syria, Commagene, Cappadocia, Metagonitis, Mauritania, and Gaetulia. The final trigon is fiery and northern, turning from the north toward the west; its images are Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius. Its Lords are Mars, the Sun, and Jupiter. To Aries and Mars are subjected Britain, part of Gaul (which is called Galatia by the Greeks), Germany, Bastarnia <note>original: "Barsania"</note>, Coele-Syria <note>original: "Concaua Syriæ," literally "Hollow Syria"</note>, Idumea, and Judea. To Leo and the Sun: Italy, Apulia, Sicily, Phoenicia, Chaldea, and the Orfenii (or Orchenii). To Sagittarius and Jupiter: Tuscany, the Celtic lands, Spain, and Arabia Felix <note>original: "fœlix Arabia"; the fertile southern region of the Arabian Peninsula</note>. These are the matters which we can hold as certain from the astronomers, and especially from Ptolemy, easily the prince of astronomers; and if there are any other regions, a subtle investigator can reconcile them with these principal ones.

### On the correspondence of the Apostles with the celestial signs. Chapter XII.

**A**nd since it is not without mystery that each region, being subject to its own sign, is assigned to one Apostle, I believe I should here examine the correspondence that each Apostle has with the sign of the region assigned to him. To do this, we must look at the proper names of the Apostles as I have been able to extract them from the most hidden monuments of the Hebrews. These names agree with the names they have in דברי הימים <note>Hebrew: *Dibre ha-Yamim*, meaning "The Words of the Days," usually referring to the Biblical books of Chronicles</note>, that is, in the "Words of the Days." 

And these names are: first, that of the prince of the Apostles himself, שמעון הכפי **Simehon hacephi** <note>Hebrew: *Shimeon ha-Kephi*</note>, who is called by us **Simeon Peter**. For Simeon is interpreted as "hearing" or "obeying." *Hacephi*, however, is "rock," and not "head" as some deceived people affirm; for it is not a Greek word <note>The author is correcting those who confused the Syriac *Kepha* (rock) with the Greek *Kephale* (head)</note>, but a Syriac word signifying a rock. 

The name of the second apostle is אלעזי **Aleuzi** <note>Hebrew: *El-uzi*</note>, that is, "God is my strength"; in place of which we have **Andrew**, which is interpreted as "answering to the pasture" <note>The author provides a common but folk-etymological interpretation of the name Andrew here</note>. 

The third is **James the Greater**, who is called by his proper name יעקבה **Iahacobah**, meaning "oppressing"; but with the letters inverted in the Hebrew manner, saying קבע **cabah**, it signifies "a helmet" or "one who is helmeted." 

The name of the fourth is פוליפוס **Polipos**, that is, "humble mouth" or "humbling of the mouth"; in place of which we have **Philip**. 

The fifth is ברכיה **Barachiah**, that is, "blessed by the Lord"; in place of which, I know not how, we have **Bartholomew**, whom they interpret as "the son of him who suspends the waters." For *Bar* is a Chaldean word <note>Aramaic</note> rather than Hebrew, and the name **Bartholomew** is never found among Hebrew names. 

The sixth is יוחנה **Iochana**, whom we call **John**, and is interpreted as "the grace of God." 

The seventh is תמני **Tamni**, who is **Thomas**, and it carries the meaning of "twin" or "didymus." 

The eighth is מדון **Medon**, that is, "judging"; in place of which we have **Matthew**, whom some interpret as "the one who is given," thinking that the name descends from the verb נתן **natan**, which means "he gave" or "bestowed." 

The ninth is **James of Alphaeus**, or **James the Less**, who is properly called עקבי **Iahacob**, which signifies "supplanter," or "tracker," or "one following footsteps." 

The tenth is **Thaddaeus**, who is called by his proper name כפשנא **Chasepha**, that is, "compressing" or "applying force," and not from תודה **Todah**, which means "praise."

He also held as his lot the region of Judea—a region distributed by lot to the chosen people. 

<margin>Peter</margin>
Symeon, who was called Cephas (that is, Peter), rightfully subjects to himself the **Lion** <note>Leo</note>, Rome, and all things directed by the Lion, the prince of beasts, having been made the Prince of the Apostles. In him the true Sun—just as the heavenly sun is here in Leo—showed its greatest power: for the true Sun <note>Christ</note> bestowed such great virtue upon him that his shadow alone conferred health upon the sick. Holding the highest peak in the Apostolic gathering and the whole Church, he possessed that power which the gates and virtues of hell would yield to. Whence he was a true Lion, of whom the Wise Man says in Proverbs: *The Lion, the most powerful of beasts, shall fear the onset of no one.* <note>original: "Leo potentiffimus beftiarũ ad nullius pauebit occurfum"</note>

<margin>James</margin>
James the Less, who is also called *Jahacobah* <note>a Latinized form of the Hebrew name Jacob</note>, meaning "one who oppresses"—but with the letters inverted is called "helmeted"—obtains the **Archer** <note>Sagittarius</note>. Having been made the protector of Spain <note>original: *Hifpaniæ*</note>, he was the oppressor of paganism, covered by the helmet of salvation, and the defender of the people of Spain, whom he undertook to protect even until now with miracles and great guardianship. Nor did he receive the protection of that people alone, but of all who flee to him, providing the benefit of his intercession to everyone. 

We have run through these things not only to demonstrate the suitability of the Apostles with the heavenly signs—by which they, being released and made "heavens" themselves, declared the glory of God everywhere—but so that we might look upon that harmonic correspondence which they have with the super-celestial signs <note>spiritual or divine archetypes beyond the physical stars</note>, and with the twelve rulers of the heavenly signs. Just as the names of those rulers were written in the gates of the heavenly city, so these Apostles, having been made the foundations matching the gates and the whole city, might adorn those very foundations with their names. For they drew their power not from the physical heavenly signs, but together with the twelve tribes from better fountains, 

<margin>Psalm</margin>
of which it is said in the Psalm: *Bless God the Lord from the fountains of Israel.* There is Benjamin, there the princes of Judah, the princes of Zebulun and Naphtali, and whichever princes belong to both the true and figurative tribes. Drawing from these fountains, both families grew in a very short time to an immense number and into spiritual gifts, but the Apostolic and Christian family much more happily; it grew not only to six hundred and three thousand, five hundred and fifty <note>The number of the Israelites in the census of the Book of Numbers</note>, but into a most copious crowd from every tribe and tongue...

### Chapter XIII.

**EVEN** if (as we have said) the Israelite people were exempt from the influence of the stars <note>The author argues that while pagans are "ruled" by astrology, Israel follows God, though still in harmony with the cosmos</note>, they were nonetheless not considered outside of their order. Hence this figurative people, to whom all things happened in symbols, was ordered to camp according to the aspects of the heavens and the signs. For toward the eastern side, where these images are—the **Twins** <note>Gemini</note>, the **Scales** <note>Libra</note>, and the **Water-Bearer** <note>Aquarius</note>—the tribes of Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun located their camps.

This Law was interpreted by a better 

<margin>Mercury</margin>

One approaches this Law through a true confession of faith, both with the heart and the mouth, as 

<margin>Paul</margin>

<margin>Isaiah</margin>

<margin>Issachar</margin>

<margin>Zebulun</margin>

<margin>Moses</margin>

<margin>Simeon</margin>

<margin>Gad</margin>

This is the sign in which the sun "girds itself" so that, proceeding backward, it may ascend again just as it had descended. For Gad was "girt from behind," as our translation has it—though it may be said differently in the truth of the literal text—concerning which it shall be spoken elsewhere. 

In the western region, where the figures of **Pisces**, **Cancer**, and **Scorpio** are depicted, the camps were located by **Ephraim**, **Manasseh**, and **Benjamin**. 

<margin>Ephraim</margin>
**Ephraim** directed his battle line near **Pisces**; this is a watery sign and exceedingly fecund, just like the nature of fish and of the waters. From this point, when the sun enters into it, the earth begins to sprout, fish pour out their eggs in the waters, and birds and animals likewise dispose themselves toward procreation. It was well for Ephraim to be encamped near a fertile sign, for his name is interpreted as "fruitful." 

<margin>Jacob</margin>

<margin>Manasseh</margin>
**Manasseh**, however, whose name they interpret as "forgetfulness," located his camp at **Cancer**. When the sun enters this sign, as if forgetting its own ascent, it moves backward, beginning to descend. <margin>Manasseh</margin>

**Benjamin** raised his standard at **Scorpio**, which is a western sign directly opposite the eastern signs, in one of which **Judah** was encamped (as is said in the books of Numbers and Joshua) when the Promised Land was being divided. The beginning of the strength of the sons of Judah is from the summit of the saltiest sea <note>the Dead Sea</note>, and from its shore, which looks toward the south; and it proceeds 

<margin>Benjamin</margin>
against the "ascent of the Scorpion" <note>A geographical pass mentioned in Joshua 15:3, the *Maaleh-acrabbim*</note>, opposite which Benjamin also located his camp. Thus, one from this side and the other from that side embracing the celestial **Scorpio**, they might prevail against the "inferior" and evil Scorpion, and against all the venoms of that serpent of whom it is said: *Dan shall be a snake upon the road, a horned serpent upon the path, biting the horse's heel, so that its rider falls backward.* 

For from the tribe of **Dan** came the horned serpent **Jeroboam**, who poisoned all Israel, leading the ten tribes into idolatry by erecting calves in Samaria, as is held in the third volume of 

<margin>Kings</margin>
**Kings**. Against this poison, only the tribes of Judah and Benjamin prevailed, persevering in the worship of the true God and adoring Him in the Temple at Jerusalem.

And most appropriately 

<margin>Dan</margin>
**Dan**, whose name is interpreted as "judgment," directs his battle line toward the north, for from the north every evil is spread abroad as a severe judgment. And he does this near **Aries** [the Ram], the animal which the Law commands to be offered for burning as an expiation for sin along with the calf, which is offered for sin, so that the judgment of God against the sinner might cease. 

**Asher**, whose name is interpreted as "riches," established his army near **Leo** and the north, from whence gold comes. For the Lion is a northern animal, robust and most ferocious. 

<margin>Asher Moses</margin>
And of Asher, **Moses** said while blessing him: *Iron and brass shall be your shoes.* These denote northern strength, as is evident to those who possess knowledge...

<margin>Jacob.</margin> And concerning his abundance and riches, the father Jacob <note>original: "Iahacob"</note> spoke: *Of Asher, his bread shall be fat, and he shall yield royal dainties.* And concerning his strength against the enemy, Moses follows: *The rider of the heaven is your helper.* And again: *He shall expel the enemy from before your face* <margin>Naphtali.</margin> *and shall say: Crush them,* namely with Leonine <note>lion-like</note> vigor. ## On the harmony of the blessings which Jacob gave to his twelve sons with the twelve peoples to whom the twelve Apostles preached, according to the order of the signs to which they correspond.

->Chapter XIV.<-

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'I' featuring floral patterns and architectural elements.</image-desc> We have now in some measure explained the harmony of both tribes—namely the figurative ones and the Apostolic family—with the celestial signs. Now let us see how harmoniously the father of both families, Israel, prophesied concerning each <margin>Israel</margin> at the end of his life. Regarding Reuben he said:
> Reuben, my firstborn, you are my strength and the beginning of my sorrow (or of my manhood); first in gifts and greatest in command.
Or as the literal truth holds:
> The remainder of the gift (or of swelling) and the remainder of strength: You are poured out like water, may you not grow, because you went up to your father’s bed and defiled his couch.
This oracle is for the most part clear enough. For he was the firstborn and the beginning of the fruit of paternal manhood. He also defiled the paternal bed because he mingled himself with Bilhah <note>original: "Bala"</note>, the concubine of his <margin>Gen.</margin> father and the handmaid of Rachel, as is held in Genesis. Wherefore he made himself utterly unworthy of celestial influence; hence his father said:
> That which was prepared for you shall not descend upon you, namely because you placed an obstacle by defiling the paternal chamber.
Whence it follows:
> The remainder of the gift and the remainder of strength, which was indeed owed to you by right of primogeniture, I do not give. For you are poured out like water, therefore there is nothing remaining that I may give you. In place of which we have: *May you not grow.*
And the reason is because you placed an obstacle, defiling the bed of your father and polluting the way or the course of ascent. These things said here of Reuben, along with those which will be said of the other sons or tribes, have their place in the <margin>CHRIST.</margin> family born of Christ the Father, of whom Jacob bore the type. Hence He, as the true father and redeemer of the true Israelite family, said:
> I am not sent except to the sheep which had perished of the house of Israel.
Concerning which house—the true and figurative rather than the prefiguring one—the ancient father Jacob spoke briefly to the elders...

Being about to depart to his own, and full of the Holy Spirit, he said to his sons: *Gather yourselves* <note>Hebrew: האספו (*he'asephu*)</note>. This does not signify "gather together," as a faulty translation has it, but rather "be increased," and "grow in merits and light," so that you may be able to grasp those deep mysteries which I wish to prophesy are coming to you in the end of time—that is, in the final age, when the Messiah shall come. Afterward follows: *Assemble yourselves* <note>Hebrew: הקבצו (*hikabzu*)</note>; that is, be joined together, not only you who are of my lineage, but all who ought to lead or serve as soldiers under God in both families <note>The author likely refers to the "two families" of the Jews and the Gentiles, or the earthly and heavenly Church</note>. celestial sign, which is Aries <note>The Ram, the first sign of the Zodiac</note>, or to the angelic or divine power presiding over it. This people inhabits Judea, Edom, the valley of Syria, Egypt (as the

Hebrews assert), Britain, Gaul <note>France</note>, and Germany. Truly, the 

<margin>Jews, Hebrews</margin>

<margin>Exodus</margin>

### Digression on why the primary order will not be preserved. Chapter XV.

**N**or will anyone wonder if we do not always follow the same order in the application of the tribes and families alongside the celestial signs and the peoples corresponding to them, since Holy Scripture itself changes the order many times. For in the blessing of the father Jacob, and in the description made upon the stones which are called <term>Urim and Thummim</term> <note>original: "urim ue tumim"; sacred objects used by the High Priest of Israel for discerning the divine will</note>, the same order is kept; but another is used in the arrangement of the camps; another in the blessing given by Moses; and another in the <term>Apocalypse</term> <note>The Book of Revelation</note>. Why this was done in both families <note>The "families" refer to the Twelve Tribes of Israel and the Twelve Apostles</note> for their own reasons and mysteries, many things would need to be said which might perhaps lead us further away than the present task requires. But lest it be believed that this happened by chance or without reason, we shall at least assign the reason why Moses, while blessing the tribes, passed over Simeon as if he had forgotten him. In his place, he put Joseph’s son Manasseh, whose name is interpreted as "forgetfulness." In this, Moses was in agreement with Jacob, who, coming to Simeon, said:
> Simeon and Levi are vessels of warring iniquity. <note>original: "Simeon, & Leui uasa iniquitatis bellantia"; Genesis 49:5</note>

> Cursed be their fury, for it is stubborn: and their indignation, for it is hard. <note>original: "Maledictus furor eorum, quia pertinax: & indignatio eorum, quia dura"; Genesis 49:7</note>
For in their fury they killed a man—namely, Hamor and his son Shechem, along with his people—and in their heart and will, they "killed" their brother Joseph. And in their self-will, they "undermined a wall" <note>The Latin *suffoderunt murum* refers to the destruction of the city of Shechem</note> or "uprooted a bull." For the Hebrew word שור (*Sor*) signifies both a wall and a bull. If, therefore, it is taken to mean "bull," it speaks of Joseph, of whom Moses said:
> His beauty is like the firstborn of a bull. <note>original: "Quasi primogeniti tauri pulchritudo eius"; Deuteronomy 33:17</note>
And lest such robust fury, gathered in those two tribes, should cause harm, the divine Patriarch continues:
> I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Israel. <note>original: "Diuidam illos in Iahacob, & dispergam eos in Israel"; Genesis 49:7</note>
And so the tribe of Levi was divided; they served the Tabernacle on behalf of all the tribes and were sustained by the tithes offered by them. He likewise did not bless Simeon, because he was not capable of receiving a blessing. Neither Moses nor his minister Joshua assigned boundaries to him when the Promised Land was divided; instead, he was placed within the boundaries of Judah. By the good and copious influence of Judah, Simeon’s "hard indignation" might be restrained, and through this fellowship, he might become capable of some good influence. However, Levi, whom Jacob would not bless, was blessed by Moses. Levi redeemed the curse given to him and earned a blessing through his great zeal for divine love, which he showed against the idolaters and worshippers of the [Golden] Calf, as we read in Exodus. For Moses, seeing the calf erected in the desert and the people playing around it, said:
> If anyone is for the Lord, let him join me. <note>original: "Si quis est Domini, iungatur mihi"; Exodus 32:26</note>
<margin>Exodus.</margin>
And all the sons of Levi gathered to him, to whom he said: "Thus says the Lord..."

### Continuation of the harmony of the blessings of Issachar and Zebulun with their peoples. Chapter XVI.

<margin>Theology</margin>
**I**ssachar <note>The text begins with a decorative woodcut initial 'I' featuring a figure in a landscape.</note>, being second in the camp-order with the second sign, which is Taurus <note>The Bull</note>, seems to me to fit. For the oracle says of him: "Issachar is a strong donkey," namely patient and robust in the study of letters, to which that tribe was dedicated. For the donkey also tastes of some kind of mercy and its influence, from which comes wisdom, as the more secret Theologians say. But letting these more hidden mysteries go for the time being, let us follow the literal sense. For one who ought to profit in learning is required to be robust; therefore, in the blessing he is likened to a donkey, and in the celestial signs to the Bull, the most robust of all cattle. He saw here rest, and the leisure of study because it was good, and the land in which the tribe itself stayed without the wandering that merchants and soldiers usually do; because it was pleasant, he therefore bowed his shoulders to carry the great burden, which is in the study of letters. And he became a servant to tribute: for Issachar served the tribe of Zebulun in a way, because the wealthy merchants provided the necessities for those of the tribe of Issachar who were occupied with the study of letters, as the Hebrews assert. Hence Moses said, while he distributed the portion of his blessing: "Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out," namely, when you go here and there...

<header>OF THE SECOND CANTICLE</header>

## OF THE SECOND CANTICLE

...you set out gathering wages; and Issachar in your tents; <note>This refers to the blessing of Moses in Deuteronomy 33:18: "Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out, and Issachar, in your tents."</note> that is to say, he will dwell there or frequent them, so that he may receive the benefits of life as a reward, just as his name indicates, which is interpreted as "wages." <note>The name Issachar is traditionally derived from the Hebrew *ish sakhar*, meaning "man of hire" or "reward."</note> If, however, these words are applied to the regions directed by the sign of Taurus, let us see: for those are the maritime regions of Asia Minor, Persia, Media, Parthia, the Cyclades, and Cyprus. In the maritime regions of Asia Minor were the seven churches to which that most famous and unique prophecy of the New Testament was dedicated—the one revealed to John on the island of Patmos (which is now called Chios <note>The author appears to confuse Patmos with the island of Chios, or reflects a contemporary geographic tradition.</note>), as is said at the beginning of the vision itself: "John to the seven churches which are in Asia: Grace to you and peace from him who was, who is, and who is to come, and from the seven spirits who are before his throne," <note>original: Revelation 1:4</note> as if those seven principal spirits took special care of those very churches, which are in Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea. Near these cities is the island of Patmos, one of the Cyclades (now called Chios), where that divine revelation took place.

And in these places, along with the surrounding regions, the study of humane letters greatly flourished; and many men most famous in learning came forth from them. From Ephesus came Heraclitus, called "the Ephesian." From the city of Scepsis, located on the mainland near Antandrus and close to Mytilene, came the Socratic philosophers Erastus and Coriscus, to whom letters written by Plato are found. There was also Neleus, the son of Coriscus; Demetrius the grammarian; and Metrodorus. From nearby Pergamum came Galen. In that same place, by the great care of the Attalid kings, a massive library was established; and in it were placed the books of Aristotle and Theophrastus by Apellicon. <note>The Library of Pergamum was the great rival to the Library of Alexandria in the ancient world.</note> For Aristotle had left his library and his school to Theophrastus; and he was the first of all the Greeks to collect books and taught the kings of Egypt the order of a library. Theophrastus then handed it over to Neleus, and Neleus brought it to Scepsis and gave it to his descendants—men who were indeed unskilled, and by whose negligence the books were ruined by dampness and gnawed by moths. <note>original: "tineis corroſi"</note> Later, they were transcribed by Apellicon, but his versions were full of errors, as <margin>Strabo</margin> Strabo reports. For this reason, the Aristotelian and Theophrastian philosophy is judged by some to be faulty, and not that polished and pure version which its authors originally handed down.

But however the matter may stand, the first library of learning after Athens (which was the mother of studies) was erected in Pergamum. Truly, because of the proximity of Athens to those maritime areas, they agreed well enough with one another, even though they are situated in the region of Greece in Europe. For between those maritime regions and Athens lie the Cyclades islands, separated only by a certain stretch of sea from both, which align both with those maritime regions directed by Taurus and with the studious tribe of Issachar. From these islands, very many famous in learning drew their origin. From Cos we have Hippocrates, and as some assert for certain, Homer. Among these is also Delos, famous for the temple and oracle of Apollo, from which their ancients received great fuel for their wisdom.

Toward the west, near Rhodes, lies Halicarnassus, famous for its <term>Dionysius</term><note>Dionysius of Halicarnassus (c. 60 BC–after 7 BC) was a Greek historian and teacher of rhetoric.</note>; from Mytilene came <term>Pittacus</term><note>One of the Seven Sages of Greece.</note>, one of the seven sages. It would be a long task to recount all the famous men who emerged from those places, and with how much labor their inhabitants devoted themselves to the study of letters. 

Moving toward Persia: there one finds <term>Magic</term><note>Latin: *Magia*. In this context, it refers to the "Wisdom of the Magi," a blend of philosophy, astronomy, and religion, rather than modern stage magic.</note>, which is a more secret philosophy, from whence came those who first worshipped Christ. From there also came <margin>Charondas; Avicenna</margin> Charondas, most excellent in that doctrine, and Avicenna <note>Ibn Sina, the famous Persian polymath and physician.</note>, as some assert. Although their school was characterized by the practice of riding and archery, as well as their fine dress, they were nonetheless not lacking in the study of letters regarding the most hidden matters; hence they were most diligent in sacred affairs. I omit many other things that could be said about the study maintained by the inhabitants of these regions, since these few examples suffice to indicate how harmoniously the celestial influences over them agree with the influence of the tribe of Issachar. His study was to devote himself to "humanly acquired" doctrine—for divinely revealed doctrine was given chiefly to the Levites.

As we follow the order of the encampments: Zebulun held the third place in the eastern region, to which we shall assign the third sign, which is Gemini <note>The Twins</note>, and the first in its triplicity. Its regions are Hyrcania, Armenia, Margiana, Cyrenaica, Marmarica, and the lower region of Egypt. Of this tribe, it was said by the father’s oracle <note>Referring to the Blessing of Jacob in Genesis 49.</note>:

> Zebulun shall dwell at the shore of the seas—and not "of the sea" as our translation has it—and he shall be at the haven of ships (add: he shall have these as his borders) and shall be extended as far as Sidon.

It is well said that he extends "to the shore of the seas," because on the eastern side he has Getulia and <margin>ומעלה</margin> *umarhala*—which our people call Magdalum, or Medala. Tiberias also stands there with its sea. On the western side, he has Mount Carmel with its port, which is now called the "Castle of the Pilgrims" <note>Château Pèlerin, a major Crusader fortress near Haifa.</note>. He also has the port of Ptolemais, which is now named Acre. He extends through the Syrian sea as far as Tyre and Sidon, even if faulty maps assign Ptolemais to the tribe of Asher. For as we have it expressly in the oracle, Zebulun extends as far as Sidon. Nor do we read of any other privilege given to this tribe except for the seas and ports through which and to which they might conduct their merchandise. 

All these things follow the regions directed by Gemini. The first of these is Hyrcania, situated by the Hyrcanian (or Caspian) Sea; Greater Armenia is also directed toward that same sea. The region of Cyrenaica likewise stretches into the sea toward Greece; while Marmarica and the region of Lower Egypt extend almost into that same sea. All these regions are occupied with the navigation and merchandise that takes place within them, just like the tribe of Zebulun, to which they correspond—unless we elevate the meanings of the oracle to higher senses and to the "supramundane sea," of which we should not speak for the present.

# SEVENTH TONE

...place among the peoples and regions subject to **Aquarius**: which are Arabia, Ethiopia, Sauromatica, Oxiana, Sogdiana, Azania, and Media. For the Arabs have no fixed region, but live within the borders of others, because there are three parts of Arabia: **Happy** <note>original: "foelix"; referring to the fertile southern region of the Arabian peninsula, modern Yemen</note>, **Desert**, and **Stony**. Indeed, the entire multitude of that nation is not contained within those lands, but extends beyond the Syrians, Phoenicians, Palestinians, and Carthaginians, always passing between the coastal peoples and the Persian, Egyptian, or Libyan deserts, through the regions of Marmarica and Cyrenaica <note>regions in modern-day Libya</note> as far as the borders of Mauritania and the Atlantic Sea. Thus, in these people, that oracle finds its place: **I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Israel** <note>Genesis 49:7; the author interprets this prophecy as applying to the broad dispersal of these groups</note>. This is understood figuratively to encompass the entire people and the number of the elect.

The dispersed and divided Arabs are the **Agarenes** <note>A medieval term for Arabs, identifying them as descendants of Hagar, the mother of Ishmael</note>, of whom the Angel of the Lord spoke to **Hagar** <margin>Genesis</margin> (as we read in Genesis) when speaking of their father, and consequently of the whole family: **He will be a wild man: his hand will be against all men, and the hands of all against him.** <note>Genesis 16:12</note> These people live by the protection of others through military skill, or they rush here and there with robberies and plunder, enriching themselves through continuous raids and the depopulation of fields, according to what that same oracle says: **His hand is against all.** For they do not build, nor do they cultivate the land, nor do they have firm dwellings, but they run to and fro carrying their homes with them, which are in fact tents; thus they seem gathered in the territories of others rather than in their own.

Following these are the **Ethiopians**, born from Cush, the son of Ham, who lead the same or even a worse life, as if they were suffering the curse which Noah gave to his descendants through their ancestor Ham, because he had wickedly mocked his father. Indeed, these people sell their own children for food. Among them are some who are not fully black, coming from the region between Egypt and Ethiopia; they wander through the entire world erecting tents outside cities in fields and at crossroads. They acquire their living through deceptions, bartering, and prognostications based on the lines of the hands <note>palmistry</note>, delighting in these frauds; they are known by the common name <term>Cingani</term> <note>original: "Cingani"; an old term for the Romani people, often historically referred to as Gypsies</note>, and they themselves are divided into various tribes.

Concerning the **Sauromatians** <note>Sarmatians</note>, or the **Hyperboreans**, whom others call the **Arimaspians**, I shall say no more than what I find written, since authors have said nothing precise about them. They are a people located in Sarmatia <note>roughly modern-day Ukraine and Southern Russia</note>, just as the **Medes** are between the Hyrcanians, Parthians, Armenians, and Persians. Media is divided into two parts; the larger is called Greater Media, whose metropolis is <term>Ecbatana</term>, which the Parthians use as a royal city, staying there in the summer because it is cool. In winter, however, they lead their lives in **Seleucia**, which is along the Tigris, near Babylon. The other part of Media is called <term>Atropatia</term> <note>Atropatene, in modern Iranian Azerbaijan</note>, named after the leader Atropates. The inhabitants there are joined by affinity to the Armenians and lie adjacent to Mariana in the east, but they are most strongly allied as confederates with the Persians. For **Ahasuerus**, whom our people call Assuerus, was King of the Persians <margin>Esther</margin> and the Medes, as we read in the Book of Esther. His rise and origin were in **Susa**, which the Hebrews call <note>Hebrew: "שׁוּשַׁן"</note> **Shushan**, but our people call **Susis**. And it is a region from the borders...

...the borders <note>completing the word 'finibus' from the previous page</note> of the Persian shores as far as the Babylonian region at the mouths of the Tigris, extending nearly three thousand stadia <note>A stadium was an ancient Greek unit of distance, roughly 185 meters or 607 feet</note>, having the Medes to the north. Concerning them, I find nothing worthy of report, except that they always learned to be subject to others, adhering to them. There remain the regions of Oxiana, Sogdiana, and Azania, situated between the Bactrians, the Massagetae, the Nomads, and that which is called the Sacred region. Since all these are obscure, they have left no memory of themselves to writers, except that they have no houses and live on livestock and milk, especially that of horses. However, in neighboring regions, within whose borders they live, some are somewhat notable: for Bactriana shines because of its **Zoroaster** <note>The ancient Iranian prophet and founder of Zoroastrianism</note>; the Massagetae because of Queen **Tomyris**, who defeated Cyrus, king of the Persians; but the towns of Azania have been destroyed along with their memory. 

The last family of that triangle <note>original: "trigoni"; referring to an astrological triplicity, a group of three zodiac signs of the same element</note> was **Gad**, who is the first son of Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid. He was Jacob's seventh son, whence his name is most appropriate, being composed of two letters signifying seven: for the Hebrews write the name itself with only two letters in this manner 
<margin>Hebrews</margin> 
**גָד** **Gad**: of which **ג** *gimel* yields three and **ד** *daleth* yields four in number; which, joined together, constitute seven. But we, following the order of the encampment, will assign him the sixth place; for we cannot follow all their various orders in a single context. 

His blessing, therefore, was: **Gad is happy**, or **good fortune will make us fortunate**: and he himself will be fortunate in the heel, or footstep. And I do not know why we have it translated as: **Gad, being girded, shall fight against him, and he himself shall be girded backward** <note>This is a critique of the Latin Vulgate translation of Genesis 49:19, which the author argues misses the pun on "fortune"</note>; for "Gad" does not mean "girded," but "happy" or "well-fortuned," as we have it explained by the mother, or by the mistress of the handmaid giving birth, who, having received this son, said **בָּא גָד** *ba gad*, that is, **in prosperity**, or **good fortune**, or as our translation has it, **happily**. His happiness, or good fortune, his father Jacob declared in the heel; but Moses traced it even to the crown of the head, saying: **Blessed be Gad in his breadth; he has couched as a lion, and the robust one shall prey even to the crown of the head.** <note>Deuteronomy 33:20</note> 

Indeed, Moses expanded and increased his influence and good fortune, because he preceded all Israel boldly and faithfully in the war against the nations which the Lord had commanded to be expelled from the land promised to that people—as we read in the book of Numbers. 
<margin>Numbers</margin> 
His good fortune was not the priesthood, nor the kingdom, nor wisdom, nor any distinction acquired by industry or genius; because (as Aristotle testifies) 
<margin>Aristotle</margin> 
where this <note>intellect or industry</note> flourishes, there is less of fortune; but rather in war, cattle, and riches, in which those who abound are commonly called fortunate. Regarding his triple riches, we read in the same place: **Reuben and Gad had many cattle, and they had great substance in beasts.** <note>Numbers 32:1</note> Therefore they wished to dwell beyond the Jordan in those most fertile pastures. 

Hence, he agrees with his sign **Capricorn**, near which he was encamped, and with the regions and peoples directed by it: which are Macedonia, Thrace, Illyria, India, Ariana, and Gedrosia. The Macedonians were fortunate in war, especially under the leadership of **Alexander**; they were also very rich in livestock and silver; therefore (as Strabo says) 
<margin>Strabo</margin> 
Philip <note>Philip II of Macedon, Alexander's father</note> established the greatest revenues there from the metals and the remaining fertility of the places.

Therefore, Ephraim was placed before him by Jacob, who was full of God, in whose birth Joseph said with a better disposition: *God has made me grow, or abound, in the land of my affliction.* <note>Genesis 41:52</note>

...we follow, having omitted the deeper mysteries which lie hidden in the inner sanctums. *Archers* <note>original: "sagittarii"</note>, or masters of arrows, *made him bitter and fought with him*—as the literal truth of the text has it—who are understood in a negative sense by Holy Scripture as those who are harsh and offensive toward their neighbor. And these were his brothers, who wanted to kill him and finally sold him. But because the Lord delivers the innocent, snatching them from the hand of those who unjustly oppress them, it follows: *His bow shall return in strength, and in the one who throws or directs his bow.* For the evils which his powerful brothers wanted to bring upon the youth Joseph recoiled upon their own heads. The reason why this happened is expressed in what follows: *The strength of his hand shall be scattered by the hand of the mighty one of Jacob* <note>original: "Iahacob"</note>, *who is the mighty God.* It follows: *Thence*—namely from God or from Israel—*shall come the shepherd of the stone of Israel.* For that is the true stone of which it is said: *And upon this rock I will build my church* <note>Matthew 16:18</note>. The shepherd is truly he who says: *I am the good shepherd* <note>John 10:11</note>. He did not proceed from Joseph, but from his father and <margin>CHRIST</margin> from God; therefore he says significantly "thence," attributing this most famous privilege to the father, which he could not attribute to the son. And lest he should seem to speak boastfully of himself, he said that he will come from thence. And because that could not happen except by the power of God, it follows: *It shall be from the God of your father and your helper, and Shaddai* <term>Shaddai: a Hebrew name for God, often translated as "Almighty"</term> (for which we have "Almighty"), and with the *blessings of the heavens above, the blessings of the abyss lying beneath, and the blessings of the breasts and of the womb.* <margin>b</margin> These things should not be believed to have been said without a mystery; for he does not speak only of the womb and breasts of women and of the growth into two tribes (for these things would be considered of little value), but the oracle hints at higher things. For from those otherworldly breasts, all the prophets flowed like milk, and from that womb which indicates piety, Abraham was blessed. Therefore, since Joseph was inferior to Abraham and did not have a prophet in his tribe or tribes nursing from those high breasts, he is blessed only with a lower blessing, which is the doubling of his family when he was granted the privilege of two tribes—one called Ephraim and the other Manasseh. Therefore it follows: *The blessings of your father are strengthened and increased above the blessings of the one conceiving* (or of the conception) *and of the doubling of the tribe.* Which blessing shall extend even to the *desire of the everlasting hills* <note>original: "collium excelsorum"</note>, or the hills of the world, or of hidden things. Because his desire would be not only for the multiplying of his family and for earthly things, but he also desired to draw something from the high hills; and he drew as much as was given to him from above. It follows: *And all these things shall be on the head of Joseph and on the crown of the Nazirite* <term>Nazarei: from the Hebrew "nazir," meaning "separated" or "consecrated." Here it refers to Joseph being set apart from his brothers.</term>—that is, the one separated from his brothers, according to what was said above: *I give to you one portion beyond your brothers.* For it was just that he who had been undeservedly expelled by his brothers should receive something separately from his father. ->TONUS SEVENTH<-

speaking of these lower things in this way: *From the fruits of the sun* <note>original: "De fructibus solis"</note>, that is, generated by the sun, and *from the fruits of the moon* <note>original: "de fructibus Lunae"</note>, namely produced by the moon (for the Sun generates, and the moon brings forth the birth); and *from the summit of the mountains of the east, and from the fruits of the hills of the world.* For the mountains of the east (which in Hebrew is called *Kedem* <note>קדם, meaning "east" or "ancient"</note>) signify the mountains of the upper region, in which the paradise of pleasure is said to have been planted. But the hills of the world signify these lower ones, from whose fruits it follows: *And from the fruits of the earth, and its fullness*—namely the fecundity of sheep. *The Inhabitant of Sinai*—that is, he who was to inhabit it and give the law on Sinai—*may he lead it upon the head of Joseph, and upon the summit of his Nazirite* <note>original: "nazarei," referring to Joseph as one "set apart" or "consecrated" among his brothers</note>, just as was recently explained. *The firstborn of the Bull*—that is, of that exalted one whom Ezekiel saw on the left of the heavenly throne <note>A reference to the "four living creatures" in Ezekiel 1:10, where the ox or bull is one of the faces</note>—is his glory or beauty. *And the horns of the unicorn are his horns*: for with those horns the animal defends itself from attackers, and with these others are defended from poison. So too was Joseph not only defended from the plots of his brothers, but from the false slander of Potiphar’s wife. He also defended his father and brothers from the destruction of a powerful famine. 

But let us return to Ephraim. He pitched camp next to the fishes <note>referring to the zodiac sign Pisces</note>. The regions belonging to this image are Lycia, Lydia, Cilicia, Pamphylia, Phazania or Hazania, as others say, Nazamonitis, and Garamantica. Lycia, Lydia, and Mysia are Mediterranean regions of Lesser Asia <note>Asia Minor</note> extending from Mount Olympus to Pamphylia, which <margin>Strabo</margin> is followed by Cilicia. They are indeed wealthy and fertile, but with boundaries so confused that they are scarcely recognized from ancient memory. For since different people have ruled there time and again, some regions were merged and others utterly overturned. After Troy was captured, the Phrygians and Mysians ruled there, then the Lydians, after them the Aeolians and Ionians, then the Persians and Macedonians, afterwards the Romans, and finally the Turks—under whom not only the Asians but many other peoples lost their languages and names at the same time. These regions, in the way they are fruitful in produce and men, agree with Ephraim, whose name is interpreted as *fruitful*. 

Cilicia is indeed famous for Tarsus and Paul: who, although he was from the tribe of Benjamin, was nevertheless born in the region corresponding to Ephraim, concerning whom that blessing was given to his father Joseph: *From thence is the shepherd of the stone of Israel.* For Paul was a universal shepherd of the sheep of the stone: who is Christ, and the true foundation of all Israel. The Garamantic region is in inner Libya beyond Marmarica up to Ethiopia, proceeding below Egypt as far as the temple of Ammon: a land which is similarly palm-bearing and watery, where the Nasamones, Psylli, and a part of the Gaetulians are located. Their regions are reported to be quite fertile, but are not well known to us in detail, because access for our people there is difficult and rare. 

Manasseh, however, pitched camp against Cancer <note>the zodiac sign of the Crab</note>. The regions of this image are Bithynia, Phrygia, Colchica, Numidia, Africa, Carthage, and Carchedonia—regions indeed not endowed with greater dignity than the oracle about Manasseh carries: for he is counted among the twelve tribes as being in second place, and himself sharing in the common portion of the blessing. <margin>Moses</margin> Nor is anything more singular said about those regions than about that family, concerning which he says...

->OF THE SECOND SONG<-

<margin>Moses</margin>
**Moses: And these are the thousands of Manasseh.** This can be understood in two ways: either because the tribe is numerous, expressed by that word "thousands," or it denotes an "influx" coming from the letter *Aleph* <note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, א</note>, which signifies "a thousand," but primarily signifies God himself, from whom all good comes. It is as if he says: "These are the things which God has granted to you, so that you may live sufficiently, abundantly, and in common life among other peoples." No other particular distinction is attributed to him. The third place in this triangle <note>A reference to the "triplicity" in astrology, where signs are grouped in threes</note> was held by Benjamin, set against the sign of Scorpio, which rules over Syria, Commagene, Cappadocia, Metagonitis, Mauritania, and Getulia. Now, the blessing given to him by his father Jacob <note>original: "Iahacob"</note> was this: *Benjamin is a ravenous wolf; in the morning he devours the prey, and in the evening he divides the spoils.* <note>Genesis 49:27</note> But Moses seems to follow this from a long distance, saying: *The most beloved of the Lord shall dwell in confidence; he shall dwell in him as if in a bridal chamber all day long, and shall rest between his shoulders.* <note>Deuteronomy 33:12</note> Truly, as is clear to one who understands well, the words of both men converge upon the same meaning:

<margin>CHRIST</margin>
Literally, both prophesied concerning Saul, the only king from the tribe of Benjamin. For he was like a wolf who secretly seized the prey; for he entered secretly into the kingdom which was owed to the tribe of Judah, and he held this from the "morning" until the "evening" of his life. And what Jacob calls "from morning until evening," Moses implies by "all day long," when he asserts that he dwells in the "bridal chamber"—that is, the royal tribunal. For when the course of his life was completed, the "prey" was divided, because the kingdom was led back to the House of David and the House of Judah, from whom it had been taken like prey during the days of Saul's life. For the kingdom had rested (says Moses) in the time of 

<margin>The same</margin>
Saul upon his shoulders; indeed, upon those shoulders of which it is said: *Saul stood taller than the others from his shoulders upward.* <note>1 Samuel 9:2</note> But let us see how this applies to the people corresponding to the tribe of Benjamin, those encamped near Scorpio. Under this image in Asia is Syria, continuous with Commagene, which receives its borders from Mount Taurus; beyond this, and following Armenia, is Cappadocia, directed by the same sign. In Africa, however, there is Metagonia (which is adjacent to New Carthage), Mauritania, and Getulia. The peoples of these lands "ate the prey in the morning," of which it is said: *To the prey, my son, you have gone up.* For the Redeemer of the world set before us heavenly food to be eaten, like a kind of "prey" snatched from the Father, or from the hands of the enemies who hinder us. These peoples ate this in the "morning," when they received the faith of the recently crucified Christ. But as the "evangelical day" turned toward evening, they "badly divided the spoils" by adhering to the most filthy Muhammad <note>original: "Mahumeti"</note>—both those peoples of Asia and those of Africa, all of whom have been divided from Christ for many ages. In this division they shall endure for a little while (as I believe), because quickly (unless I am mistaken) that day will come, by God's approach, in which there shall be "one fold and one shepherd." These peoples were divided in one way, but in another way not at all, just as we read concerning that ancient and symbolic family in the third book of Kings <note>Known today as 1 Kings</note>, in which ten tribes were divided from the House of Judah, where the kingdom and the temple remained.

...and from the rule of the Davidic line: For just as they were not entirely abandoned, even though they were found to be apostates in the worship of the calves <note>A reference to the golden calves set up by King Jeroboam in the Northern Kingdom of Israel, an act of idolatry mentioned in 1 Kings 12</note>; since prophets were sent to those kings to direct and instruct those peoples, so that God might always rule in Jacob. ### On the harmony of the blessings of the remaining tribes which are encamped against the fourth trigon <term>trigon: a triangle formed by three zodiac signs of the same element; in this case, the author is grouping tribes with astrological signs</term> with the peoples directed by it. Chapter XX.

<margin>Moses</margin>
<margin>Strabo, Ptolemy</margin>
**I**n the fourth triad of signs, Dan, Asher, and Naphtali placed their camps. For Dan corresponds with the peoples directed by the Virgin <note>the zodiac sign Virgo</note>, who are the Greeks, Achaeans, Cretans, Babylonians, Mesopotamians, Assyrians, and Elamites. For Greece, extending its wider boundaries (as geographers assign), goes from the Bosphorus all the way to Acarnania, which includes Achaia (which they call Phthia), and also Crete with many adjacent islands. In these regions, the study of letters, acquired by human genius, flourished. No less so in the Babylonian region, whose beginning is from the east at Susa, as Strabo reports and Ptolemy shows: on the north it is surrounded by the Euphrates; on another part by Arabia; and on the north <note>The author uses both "aquilo" and "septentrio" for northern directions</note> it is bounded by the Armenians. This region so glowed with studies, especially mathematical ones, that the Babylonians were even divided into several sects. For some of them, called Chaldeans, professing the art of casting horoscopes <term>Genethlialogy: the branch of astrology dealing with the prediction of a person's life based on their birth chart</term>, were divided into the Orcheni and the Borispeni. These Borispeni are named after the city of Borispa <note>Borsippa, an ancient Mesopotamian city</note>, dedicated to Diana and Apollo. Mesopotamia is situated between the Tigris and the Euphrates, a region very rich in pastures, bordering the Babylonian province, and thus a participant in its learning. Here indeed Abraham, easily the prince of all true astronomers, first learned divine astrology from men, but more perfectly through divine illumination <note>In many Renaissance traditions, the patriarch Abraham was credited with discovering the secrets of the stars and teaching them to the civilizations of the Near East.</note>. Bordering them are the Assyrians and Elamites, filled with no small wisdom, as is proved in John of Damascus, Pherecydes the Syrian, Bardasanes, Eusebius of Caesarea, and many others. For these were most famous men after the Apostles and Prophets, who were also Assyrians themselves. But we do not number these among those wise in the doctrine acquired by human genius, since their wisdom far exceeded the human. Concerning these peoples, therefore, and their leaders who were occupied with human wisdom, it can be said what Jacob says of Dan:
<margin>Jacob</margin>
<margin>Moses</margin>
**Dan shall judge his people**, like one of the other tribes <note>Genesis 49:16</note>; because indeed among these peoples there shall be wise men for judging. Moses pursues the same thing, although he uses other words. For he says: **Dan is a lion’s whelp** <note>Deuteronomy 33:22</note>. For he himself was not a fierce kingly lion like Judah, concerning whom it is written: *The lion of the tribe of Judah has conquered* <note>Revelation 5:5</note>; but he is called a lion’s whelp, as if the son of a king. For to no tribe...

the true kingdom was given to none but the tribe of Judah; for the others, it was given only through a certain participation in that royal inheritance. As for what follows regarding Jacob, when he says: *Dan shall be a serpent in the way, a horned snake in the path biting the horse's hooves, so that his rider falls backward* <note>original: "Erit Dan coluber in uia..." - a quote from Genesis 49:17</note>, all of this refers to Samson, who was from the tribe of Dan. He was indeed a wondrous and astounding example of might and strength. For he "bit the hooves and the feet of the horse"—that is, the strength of the Philistines—when he tore out the columns of the palace which supported it like feet, causing the princes and the most distinguished men of the Philistines who were present there to fall. But since all these things were decreed by God, there follows: *Thy salvation*—so that you may be saved from these falls—or, *Thy salvation*—meaning you shall expect your strength from the Lord. In our version we have: *I will wait for thy salvation, O Lord.* Moses explains this in other words, saying: *It shall flow*—namely, this strength of yours—*abundantly from Bashan* <note>Bashan was a region famous for its fertile pastures and cattle; the author interprets this "fatness" as a spiritual or supernatural abundance</note>, that is, from that supramundane fatness from which every best gift comes. 

There are also those who interpret this oracle differently, namely concerning the Antichrist, whom they believe will be born from the tribe of Dan. He will be a "heresiarch" <term>heresiarch: a leader of a heretical sect</term> and a twisting serpent making all those whom he bites fall. His power will "flow from Bashan," meaning from the dryness of grace and the fatness of temporal things; for "Bashan" can signify both <note>The author plays on Hebrew etymologies where Bashan can be linked to both fertility/fatness and a sense of "shame" or "confusion" depending on the root</note>. For this reason, they believe this tribe of Dan was omitted by John in the numbering of the sealed <note>A reference to Revelation 7, where Dan is famously left out of the list of the twelve tribes of Israel who receive the seal of God</note>, lest the origin of such great wickedness be counted in the number of the blessed. For he "bites those horses" of which 

<margin>Habakkuk</margin> 

Habakkuk speaks: *You who mount upon your horses* <note>Habakkuk 3:8</note>, who are held in check by the bit and bridle of true discipline and the power of the divine name, of which it is not permitted to speak at present.

To Asher, however, we shall assign **Libra** <note>The Scales</note>, whose regions are Bactriana, Caspiria, Syria, Thebais, Oaxis, and the Troglodytic region. **Bactriana** is bounded by the Oxus river to the north and east; to the south it shares a border with the Arians, with the Caucasus mountains interceding; to the north lie the Margians and Hyrcanians. It is fertile with dromedaries and elephants, and quite happy with an abundance of other things. Furthermore, it was celebrated for its King Pharaotes by Philostratus, and for Zoroaster by many others. **Caspiria** is not far distant from Bactriana, famous for its mountain and the Caspian Sea; its inhabitants are exceedingly impious toward their parents, for when they reach their seventieth year, they kill them through hunger and starvation. All of **Syria** is bounded on the north by Cilicia and Mount Amanus; toward the east by the Euphrates; to the south by Arabia Felix; and from the west by the Egyptian and Cyprian seas—a region indeed distinguished by much prosperity. **Thebais** lies between the Nile river and the Libyan mountains, after which the **Oaxites** extend as far as the "Fountain of the Sun" and beyond. The **Troglodytic** region <note>The "land of the cave-dwellers," usually placed by ancient geographers along the Red Sea coast</note> stretches in a line along the Arabian Gulf as far as Mount Elephant. The life of the inhabitants is pastoral; they hold wives and children in common, except for those belonging to the tyrants, of whom many are found among them. If anyone corrupts the wives of these men, he is fined one sheep. But let us see how well those things coincide with these peoples, which were said concerning...

CCCXXIIII

->THE SEVENTH TONE<-

<margin>Jacob. Moses</margin>
Asher provides an oracle: for Jacob says: *Asher, his bread shall be fat, and he shall yield dainties for kings.* <note>original: "Asher pinguis panis eius..." — from Genesis 49:20</note> And Moses says: *Let Asher be blessed with children; let him be pleasing to his brothers, and let him dip his foot in oil. Iron and brass shall be his shoe; as the days of his youth, so also shall be his old age.* <note>original: "Benedictus in filiis Asher..." — from Deuteronomy 33:24–25</note> The "fatness of food" attributed to him refers to those regions which are fertile, and therefore peaceful among their brothers and fellow countrymen. However, what is said regarding *iron and brass being his shoe* refers to the Caspian peoples, who are said to be cruel and impious toward their parents. Furthermore, the fact that the days of youth are made equal to old age indicates that those regions underwent few or no changes, but followed the same customs through different ages: for the same religious worship, character, and manners have existed among them almost forever. 

We shall indeed assign Naphtali to Sagittarius <note>The author is linking the twelve tribes of Israel to the twelve signs of the Zodiac; Naphtali is here paired with the Archer</note>: whose regions are Tuscany, Colchis, Spain, and <term>Arabia Felix: "Happy" or "Fertile" Arabia, the southern part of the Arabian Peninsula known in antiquity for its wealth and spices</term>. Tuscany, situated between the Tyrrhenian Sea and the river Tiber, is filled with many noble and seasonal fruits, but is easily deceptive. The region of Colchis lies between Iberia <note>This refers to Caucasian Iberia, modern-day Georgia, not the Spanish peninsula</note> and the Euxine Sea <note>The Black Sea</note>, and is separated from it by the Caucasus Mountains. By the river Corax it is distinguished on the northern side from Asiatic Sarmatia; but on the western side by Mount Moschius, being a neighbor to the people of Trapezus. In that part which faces the Sarmatian plains, it is very rich in every kind of forest, especially those trees which are suitable for building ships. 

Deserts of the other Arabia distinguish "Happy Arabia" from the north; from the east, the Persian Gulf; from the west, the Arabian Gulf; and from the south, the Great Sea, which lies outside both gulfs. It is "Happy" indeed because of its many gums and fragrances, and such great wealth that Alexander the Macedonian was delighted by it in a wonderful way, as historians have recorded. But it was even happier because the Law was given on Mount Sinai—not without a mystery, which Paul

<margin>Paul</margin>
the Apostle hints at, though he does not fully explain, when he says: *Sinai is a mountain in Arabia, joined to that which is now Jerusalem, which is our mother.* <note>referencing Galatians 4:25–26</note> For the words of the Apostle are deeper than they sound in the voice. To the south of the Sardinian people, Spain has the sea; from the west it has the Atlantic all the way to the north, in which part it is indeed forested and harmful; but from the south, almost the whole land is most fertile and happy. Let us see if the blessing of Naphtali fits these regions:

<margin>Jacob. Moses</margin>
for Jacob said: *Naphtali is a hind let loose, giving goodly words.* <note>original: "Nephtalim ceruus emissus..." — from Genesis 49:21</note> But Moses says: *Naphtali shall enjoy abundance, and shall be full with the blessings of the Lord; he shall possess the sea and the south.* <note>Deuteronomy 33:23</note> For the explanation of this text, it must be known that the firstfruits were always harvested from the land of Naphtali, which were offered as the first-fruits to the Lord. In this offering, pleasant and beautiful praises were paid to God. Therefore, Jacob says that he "gives goodly words," with which Moses says he "enjoys abundance" and is "full of blessings," and "possesses the sea and the south"—that is, the super-celestial realm, from which comes all blessing, generosity, and affluence; where there is also the most hidden power of the "high-leaping hinds," who are adjured in the Song [of Songs]...

CCCXXXIII

->OF THE SECOND SONG<-

<warning>Faded text in top margin and ink bleed-through from the verso page. Slight shadow on the right edge.</warning>

...prophecies: Therefore Jacob calls him a **hind let loose** <note>original: "ceruum emissum" — from Genesis 49:21</note>, because from that comes his strength and abundance. Once the region assigned to Naphtali was made fertile, it provided more seasonal fruits than other regions, providing the first fruits to be offered to God; and from there, the most beautiful praises and eloquent words were paid to Him. **Arabia Felix** <note>Ancient term for the southern Arabian Peninsula, known for its fertility and wealth in spices</note> also provides frankincense and incense, with which we are accustomed to pay solemn praises to God and direct prayers toward Him together with the incense itself, so that it can also be said of that region: *He gives words of beauty.* **Tuscany** and **Spain** also produce seasonal fruits; especially that region of the latter which has the Mediterranean Sea to the south, according to that Mosaic prophecy: <margin>Moses</margin> *He shall possess the sea and the south.* <note>original: "Mare & meridiem possidebit" — from Deuteronomy 33:23</note> I see very little way that this can be preserved according to the literal sense, although some less skilled in the description of the world have said certain foolish things—namely, that the tribe itself perhaps held territory by the Sea of Tiberias <note>The Sea of Galilee</note>. This cannot stand at all, since the tribe of Issachar and a certain arm of the tribe of Manasseh fall between that sea and the tribe of Naphtali. Nor is there any lack of those who say even more foolishly that the tribe itself had its lot by the Tyrrhenian Sea; such people offer themselves as objects of ridicule rather than as ones to be refuted. Nor can the literal text be verified regarding the Syrian Sea, since it holds very little of it, and this on the western side. For the maritime tribe of Dan occupies the coast as far as the tribe of Simeon and Philistia. Therefore, the truth of the Mosaic oracle must be sought elsewhere, since it cannot be found in the **husk of the letter** <note>A common medieval metaphor for the literal meaning of a text versus its deeper spiritual "kernel"</note>. Indeed, according to the <term>anagogical sense: an interpretation that finds a spiritual or mystical meaning related to the afterlife or the divine realm</term>, it possesses the "supra-mundane" sea and the true South, and the southern wind blowing through, from which it receives a large abundance and seasonal fruits. However, in our <term>allegorical sense: a symbolic interpretation where people or events represent deeper moral or spiritual meanings</term>, it signifies the Spanish region, which from the Pyrenean mountains all the way to the Pillars of Hercules enjoys that Sardinian sea in the southern region, which is even more fertile than the other regions of the Spains. For these Spaniards, the oracle can be accommodated according to both the letter and the etymology of the name, so that they may rightly be called **hinds let loose**, since they are very swift, agile, and slender, just like hinds. This is also indicated by the <note>original: "interpretatio chaldaica"</note> **Aramaic interpretation** <note>Refers to the Targums, ancient Aramaic translations and paraphrases of the Hebrew Bible which often expanded on the text</note>: for "Spaniards" is interpreted as "those girt up" or "the unencumbered." They also give **words of beauty**, since their speech is wandering and charming, perhaps from <margin>Astro- <br/> nomy</margin> Jupiter and Sagittarius, as the astronomers would say. We could bring forward many other things for the harmony of these matters, but let these few suffice for discovering rather than fully explaining such mysteries, since the latter is impossible: for many things greater than these are hidden, which we partly do not see and partly are not permitted to speak of.

# THE SEVENTH TONE.

### CCCXV

...because to him was entrusted the care not just of one, but of all the churches, as a universal shepherd or a <term>chosen vessel<note>original: "uasi electo" — a reference to Acts 9:15, where God calls Paul a "chosen vessel" to carry His name before the Gentiles</note></term> for the salvation of all nations, just as he himself says when discussing the Corinthians: <margin>Paul</margin> *My daily pressure, and the care for all the churches.* <note>original: "Instantia mea quotidiana, & sollicitudo omnium ecclesiarũ" — from 2 Corinthians 11:28</note> Just as also the royal Prophet, <margin>David</margin> full of the Holy Spirit, sings in a triumphant song, saying: *In the churches*—namely, for us gathered from all the tribes—*bless God the Lord from the fountains of Israel* <note>original: "In ecclesiis... benedicite Deo Domino de fontibus Israel" — from Psalm 68:26</note>; from the twelve Apostolic fountains, to be sure, whose type was carried by the twelve tribes and their twelve springs at **Elim**. <note>A site mentioned in Exodus 15:27 where the Israelites found twelve springs of water</note> But because those figurative springs were destined to fail, they are rightly called "failing" when representing them: for **Elim** is interpreted as "failing." <note>The author uses a traditional medieval etymology where 'Elim' is linked to a lack or deficiency of the Old Law compared to the New</note> However, the true and figurative fountains by no means fail, but (as the Supreme Truth bears witness) from them flows water, and living springs leaping up into eternal life, continually irrigating the regions entrusted to them.

Thus Peter was a fountain, James was a fountain, John was a fountain—finally, all the Apostles were fountains, each one irrigating his own family. Paul, however, the most abundant fountain of all, irrigated everyone. Hence the Prophet follows: *There*, that is, in all those churches, *is Benjamin, the youth, in ecstasy of mind* <note>original: "Beniamin adolescentulus in mentis excessu" — from Psalm 68:27</note>, having been caught up even to the third heaven and those lofty breasts from which he drew the milk and water that he would offer to all the churches. For this reason, everyone interprets this **Benjamin** as Paul, who was both descended from his family, and because those things which the oracle brings forth are verified word-for-word concerning him. For the Patriarch <margin>Jacob</margin> **Jacob** said: *Benjamin is a ravenous wolf; in the morning he shall devour the prey, and at evening he shall divide the food.* <note>original: "Beniamin lupus rapax mane rapiet prædam, & uespere diuidet escas" — from Genesis 49:27</note> He was indeed a devourer in the beginning of his life, when he persecuted the church of God; but in the evening, growing old, he so divided the food and the spoils <margin>Paul</margin> that he could say: *I have become all things to all men, that I might win them for Christ.*

I also think the two-fold name suited to both should be noted: for that last son of our Patriarch Jacob was first called **Benoni**, that is, "son of my sorrow," because his mother bore him in extreme pain. Afterward, he was named by his father **Benjamin**, that is, "son of the right hand." It was no different for Paul, who was first the "son of sorrow" for the church while he sharply persecuted it even to its utter destruction, had it been permitted to him from above. But, warned by the voice of Christ, he was changed into another man and made a true "son of the right hand"; for he received Him who calls—whose proper seat is at the right hand of God the Father—into the innermost parts of his heart with all his strength, so that he no longer <margin>The same [Paul]</margin> lived for himself, but rather for his guest, saying: *I live, now not I, but Christ lives in me.* <note>original: "Viuo ego iam non ego, uiuit uero in me Christus" — from Galatians 2:20</note> Nor did he then speak of himself, since Christ suggested the words to him, as he testifies elsewhere: <margin>The same [Paul]</margin> *Do you seek proof of Christ, who speaks in me?* <note>original: "An experimentum quæritis eius, qui in me loquitur Christus?" — from 2 Corinthians 13:3</note> Hence, not without mystery, Paul, having now been made the "son of the right hand," is placed at the right hand of Peter, not only by painters—to whom, as with poets, <margin>Horace</margin> *there has always been an equal power of daring anything* <note>original: "Quidlibet audendi semper fuit æqua potestas" — a famous quote from Horace’s Ars Poetica</note>—but even on the seals of apostolic documents. Nor do I think that Blessed **Sylvester**...

...and those ancient fathers, who were entirely vigilant in ecclesiastical discipline, did not permit this order of such great princes to occur by chance or without consideration in the apostolic seals. Instead, being filled with God and looking upon sacred mysteries, they purposefully placed on the right hand him who fought the wars of the Prince’s right hand, who is Christ JESUS. He was a very strenuous soldier and, laboring more than all others, he enrolled countless fellow soldiers for his Emperor, whom he had gathered from various peoples, nations, and tribes; for which reason he was also called the "Teacher of the Gentiles" by the supreme Emperor. For he preached, as he himself says, the gospel of Christ where Christ <margin>Isaiah</margin> was not even named, just as it is written: *For those to whom he was not announced shall see: and those who have not heard of him shall understand.* <note>original: "Quoniā, quibus non eſt annuntiatum de eo, uidebunt: & qui non audierūt de eo, intelligent." — Romans 15:21, quoting Isaiah 52:15</note> Therefore, to bring the gospel to the nations, he went to the Arabs, Greeks, Italians, and Spaniards, traveling through the regions of diverse peoples across a great part of the world. Finally, with Peter, the Prince of the Apostles, he undertook the care of the universal church, favoring the power of the right hand of the divine word, just as Peter sustained the same with the left hand of the judgment entrusted to him. Hence, the former is decorated with the <term>sword of the spirit<note>A common attribute of St. Paul, representing the Word of God</note></term>, which is the word of God, and the latter with the <term>keys of judgment<note>The traditional attribute of St. Peter, representing the power to "bind and loose"</note></term> on noble heraldic shields. Encompassing Christ from both sides, they followed Him, who always held the middle position in the ecclesiastical kingdom, even though proceeding from the Father’s right hand He returned there again. And because they were joined in their pilgrimage and killed together for Christ, they also reign together.

There, then, is **Benjamin** in an <term>ecstasy of mind<note>original: "mentis excessu" — referencing Paul's mystical experience in 2 Corinthians 12</note></term>, because being elevated to heavenly things, he saw the secrets of God which it is not permitted for man to speak. And with this illustrious master of the army, not without mystery, are numbered the princes of **Judah**, the princes of **Zebulun**, and the princes of **Naphtali**, so that by these may be understood all the princes and soldiers who fight against the various throngs of our enemies, which are reduced to a <term>triple battle line<note>A reference to the "triple enemy" of the soul: the world, the flesh, and the devil, or the three lusts mentioned in 1 John 2:16</note></term> by John and by our wise men. For the prince of the military of faith and of due submission against the battle line of pride is sung as **Judah**, who, interpreted as "praise" and "confession," rules those who, confessing God with heart and mouth, recognize Him as the Lord and the teacher of all good things.

The prince of the troop of hope is called **Zebulun**, which signifies a "dwelling of strength," in which the gathered soldiers, fortified by the protection of hope, fear the hardship and horror of war not at all. The prince of charity, however, is **Naphtali**, which signifies "extension" or more truly (as we touched upon above) "equality." For charity dilates the heart and all things, and makes all things equal. And this troop is raised up against greed, hatred, factions, and all things hostile to true peace, just as the bulwarks of hope are raised against enervating and soft lewdness. Thus, under the great and distinguished leader **Paul**, and the supreme Emperor **Christ**, we all—a three-part troop—fight against the three-headed enemy and that immense and dire **Cerberus**. <note>The three-headed dog of Hades, used here to represent the Devil or the complexity of the "triple enemy" mentioned above</note> Therefore, to Paul, as the master of the entire army, not one particular church but the universal church is assigned, just as to Peter, established as judge by the supreme Prince, the jurisdiction of the entire <term>Christian Republic<note>original: "Rei-publicae Christianae" — a term for the collective body of Christendom</note></term> is entrusted.
